12870.label: Job 1:1
12870.text: There happened to be a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job; and that man proved to be blameless and upright, and fearing God and turning aside from bad.

12871.label: Job 1:2
12871.text: And seven sons and three daughters came to be born to him.

12872.label: Job 1:3
12872.text: And his livestock got to be seven thousand sheep and three thousand camels and five hundred spans of cattle and five hundred she-asses, along with a very large body of servants; and that man came to be the greatest of all the Orientals.

12873.label: Job 1:4
12873.text: And his sons went and held a banquet at the house of each one on his own day; and they sent and invited their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

12874.label: Job 1:5
12874.text: And it would occur that when the banquet days had gone round the circuit, Job would send and sanctify them; and he got up early in the morning and offered up burnt sacrifices according to the number of all of them; for, said Job, “maybe my sons have sinned and have cursed God in their heart.” That is the way Job would do always.

12875.label: Job 1:6
12875.text: Now it came to be the day when the sons of the [true] God entered to take their station before Jehovah, and even Satan proceeded to enter right among them.

12876.label: Job 1:7
12876.text: Then Jehovah said to Satan: “Where do you come from?” At that Satan answered Jehovah and said: “From roving about in the earth and from walking about in it.”

12877.label: Job 1:8
12877.text: And Jehovah went on to say to Satan: “Have you set your heart upon my servant Job, that there is no one like him in the earth, a man blameless and upright, fearing God and turning aside from bad?”

12878.label: Job 1:9
12878.text: At that Satan answered Jehovah and said: “Is it for nothing that Job has feared God?

12879.label: Job 1:10
12879.text: Have not you yourself put up a hedge about him and about his house and about everything that he has all around? The work of his hands you have blessed, and his livestock itself has spread abroad in the earth.

12880.label: Job 1:11
12880.text: But, for a change, thrust out your hand, please, and touch everything he has [and see] whether he will not curse you to your very face.”

12881.label: Job 1:12
12881.text: Accordingly Jehovah said to Satan: “Look! Everything that he has is in your hand. Only against him himself do not thrust out your hand!” So Satan went out away from the person of Jehovah.

12882.label: Job 1:13
12882.text: Now it came to be the day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their brother the firstborn.

12883.label: Job 1:14
12883.text: And there came a messenger to Job, and he proceeded to say: “The cattle themselves happened to be plowing and the she-asses were grazing at the side of them

12884.label: Job 1:15
12884.text: when the Sa·beʹans came making a raid and taking them, and the attendants they struck down with the edge of the sword; and I got to escape, only I by myself, to tell you.”

12885.label: Job 1:16
12885.text: While this one was yet speaking that one came and proceeded to say: “The very fire of God fell from the heavens and went blazing among the sheep and the attendants and eating them up; and I got to escape, only I by myself, to tell you.”

12886.label: Job 1:17
12886.text: While that one was yet speaking another one came and proceeded to say: “The Chal·deʹans made up three bands and went dashing against the camels and taking them, and the attendants they struck down with the edge of the sword; and I got to escape, only I by myself, to tell you.”

12887.label: Job 1:18
12887.text: While this other one was yet speaking, still another one came and proceeded to say: “Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their brother the firstborn.

12888.label: Job 1:19
12888.text: And, look! there came a great wind from the region of the wilderness, and it went striking the four corners of the house, so that it fell upon the young people and they died. And I got to escape, only I by myself, to tell you.”

12889.label: Job 1:20
12889.text: And Job proceeded to get up and rip his sleeveless coat apart and cut the hair off his head and fall to the earth and bow down

12890.label: Job 1:21
12890.text: and say: “Naked I came out of my mother’s belly, And naked shall I return there. Jehovah himself has given, and Jehovah himself has taken away. Let the name of Jehovah continue to be blessed.”

12891.label: Job 1:22
12891.text: In all this Job did not sin or ascribe anything improper to God.

12892.label: Job 2:1
12892.text: Afterward it came to be the day when the sons of the [true] God entered to take their station before Jehovah, and Satan also proceeded to enter right among them to take his station before Jehovah.

12893.label: Job 2:2
12893.text: Then Jehovah said to Satan: “Just where do you come from?” At that Satan answered Jehovah and said: “From roving about in the earth and from walking about in it.”

12894.label: Job 2:3
12894.text: And Jehovah went on to say to Satan: “Have you set your heart upon my servant Job, that there is no one like him in the earth, a man blameless and upright, fearing God and turning aside from bad? Even yet he is holding fast his integrity, although you incite me against him to swallow him up without cause.”

12895.label: Job 2:4
12895.text: But Satan answered Jehovah and said: “Skin in behalf of skin, and everything that a man has he will give in behalf of his soul.

12896.label: Job 2:5
12896.text: For a change, thrust out your hand, please, and touch as far as his bone and his flesh [and see] whether he will not curse you to your very face.”

12897.label: Job 2:6
12897.text: Accordingly Jehovah said to Satan: “There he is in your hand! Only watch out for his soul itself!”

12898.label: Job 2:7
12898.text: So Satan went out away from the person of Jehovah and struck Job with a malignant boil from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head.

12899.label: Job 2:8
12899.text: And he proceeded to take for himself a fragment of earthenware with which to scrape himself; and he was sitting in among the ashes.

12900.label: Job 2:9
12900.text: Finally his wife said to him: “Are you yet holding fast your integrity? Curse God and die!”

12901.label: Job 2:10
12901.text: But he said to her: “As one of the senseless women speaks, you speak also. Shall we accept merely what is good from the [true] God and not accept also what is bad?” In all this Job did not sin with his lips.

12902.label: Job 2:11
12902.text: And three companions of Job got to hear of all this calamity that had come upon him, and they proceeded to come, each one from his own place, Elʹi·phaz the Teʹman·ite and Bilʹdad the Shuʹhite and Zoʹphar the Naʹa·ma·thite. So they met together by appointment to come and sympathize with him and comfort him.

12903.label: Job 2:12
12903.text: When they raised their eyes from far off they did not then recognize him. And they proceeded to raise their voice and weep and rip each one his sleeveless coat apart and toss dust toward the heavens upon their heads.

12904.label: Job 2:13
12904.text: And they kept sitting with him on the earth seven days and seven nights, and there was no one speaking a word to him, for they saw that the pain was very great.

12905.label: Job 3:1
12905.text: It was after this that Job opened his mouth and began to call down evil upon his day.

12907.label: Job 3:3
12907.text: “Let the day perish on which I came to be born, Also the night that someone said, ‘An able-bodied man has been conceived!’

12908.label: Job 3:4
12908.text: As for that day, let it become darkness.Let not God look for it from above,Nor let daylight beam upon it.

12909.label: Job 3:5
12909.text: Let darkness and deep shadow reclaim it.Let a rain cloud reside over it.Let the things that darken a day terrorize it.

12910.label: Job 3:6
12910.text: That night—let gloom take it; Let it not feel glad among the days of a year;Among the number of the lunar months let it not enter.

12911.label: Job 3:7
12911.text: Look! That night—let it become sterile;Let no joyful cry come in it.

12912.label: Job 3:8
12912.text: Let cursers of the day execrate it,Those ready to awaken Le·viʹa·than.

12913.label: Job 3:9
12913.text: Let the stars of its twilight grow dark;Let it wait for the light and there be none;And let it not see the beams of dawn.

12914.label: Job 3:10
12914.text: For it did not close the doors of my [mother’s] belly, And so conceal trouble from my eyes.

12915.label: Job 3:11
12915.text: Why from the womb did I not proceed to die? [Why did I not] come forth from the belly itself and then expire?

12916.label: Job 3:12
12916.text: Why was it that knees confronted me,And why breasts that I should take suck?

12917.label: Job 3:13
12917.text: For by now I should have lain down that I might be undisturbed; I should have slept then; I should be at rest

12918.label: Job 3:14
12918.text: With kings and counselors of the earth, Those building desolate places for themselves,

12919.label: Job 3:15
12919.text: Or with princes who have gold,Those who fill their houses with silver;

12920.label: Job 3:16
12920.text: Or, like a hidden miscarriage, I should not come to be,Like children that have seen no light.

12921.label: Job 3:17
12921.text: There the wicked themselves have ceased from agitation, And there those weary in power are at rest.

12922.label: Job 3:18
12922.text: Together prisoners themselves are at ease;They actually do not hear the voice of one driving them to work.

12923.label: Job 3:19
12923.text: Small and great are there the same, And the slave is set free from his master.

12924.label: Job 3:20
12924.text: Why does he give light to one having trouble,And life to those bitter of soul?

12925.label: Job 3:21
12925.text: Why are there those waiting for death, and it is not, Although they keep digging for it more than for hidden treasures?

12926.label: Job 3:22
12926.text: Those who are rejoicing to gleefulness, They exult because they find a burial place.

12927.label: Job 3:23
12927.text: [Why does he give light] to able-bodied man, whose way has been concealed, And whom God hedges in?

12928.label: Job 3:24
12928.text: For before my food my sighing comes, And like waters my roaring cries pour forth;

12929.label: Job 3:25
12929.text: Because a dreadful thing I have dreaded, and it comes upon me;And what I have been scared of comes to me.

12930.label: Job 3:26
12930.text: I have not been carefree, nor have I been undisturbed,Nor been at rest, and yet agitation comes.”

12931.label: Job 4:1
12931.text: And Elʹi·phaz the Teʹman·ite proceeded to reply and say:

12932.label: Job 4:2
12932.text: “If one does try out a word to you, will you become weary?But to put a restraint on words who is able?

12933.label: Job 4:3
12933.text: Look! You have corrected many, And the weak hands you used to strengthen.

12934.label: Job 4:4
12934.text: Anyone stumbling, your words would raise up; And knees giving way you would make firm.

12935.label: Job 4:5
12935.text: But this time it comes to you, and you become weary;It touches even you, and you get disturbed.

12936.label: Job 4:6
12936.text: Is not your reverence [the basis of] your confidence?Is not your hope even the integrity of your ways?

12937.label: Job 4:7
12937.text: Remember, please: Who that is innocent has ever perished?And where have the upright ever been effaced?

12938.label: Job 4:8
12938.text: According to what I have seen, those devising what is hurtfulAnd those sowing trouble will themselves reap it.

12939.label: Job 4:9
12939.text: Through the breath of God they perish,And through the spirit of his anger they come to an end.

12940.label: Job 4:10
12940.text: There is the roaring of a lion, and the voice of a young lion,But the teeth of maned young lions do get broken down.

12941.label: Job 4:11
12941.text: A lion is perishing from there being no prey,And the cubs of a lion are separated from one another.

12942.label: Job 4:12
12942.text: Now to me a word was stealthily brought,And my ear proceeded to get a whisper of it,

12943.label: Job 4:13
12943.text: In disquieting thoughts from visions of the night,When deep sleep falls upon men.

12944.label: Job 4:14
12944.text: A dread came over me, and a trembling,And the multitude of my bones it filled with dread.

12945.label: Job 4:15
12945.text: And a spirit itself went passing over my face;The hair of my flesh began to bristle.

12946.label: Job 4:16
12946.text: It began to stand still,But I did not recognize its appearance;A form was in front of my eyes;There was a calm, and I now heard a voice:

12947.label: Job 4:17
12947.text: ‘Mortal man —can he be more just than God himself?Or can able-bodied man be cleaner than his own Maker?’

12948.label: Job 4:18
12948.text: Look! In his servants he has no faith,And his messengers he charges with faultiness.

12949.label: Job 4:19
12949.text: How much more so with those dwelling in houses of clay,Whose foundation is in the dust! One crushes them more quickly than a moth.

12950.label: Job 4:20
12950.text: From morning to evening they are crushed to pieces;Without anyone’s taking [it to heart] they perish forever.

12951.label: Job 4:21
12951.text: Has not their tent cord within them been pulled out?They die for lack of wisdom.

12952.label: Job 5:1
12952.text: “Call, please! Is there anyone answering you?And to which one of the holy ones will you turn?

12953.label: Job 5:2
12953.text: For the foolish one vexation will kill,And the one easily enticed envying will put to death.

12954.label: Job 5:3
12954.text: I myself have seen the foolish one taking root, But suddenly I began to execrate his abiding place.

12955.label: Job 5:4
12955.text: His sons remain far from salvation, And they are crushed in the gate without a deliverer.

12956.label: Job 5:5
12956.text: What he harvests the hungry one eats;And even from butcher hooks one takes it,And a snare actually snaps at their means of maintenance.

12957.label: Job 5:6
12957.text: For not from mere dust does what is hurtful go forth,And from mere ground trouble does not spring up.

12958.label: Job 5:7
12958.text: For man himself is born for trouble,As the very sparks fly upward.

12959.label: Job 5:8
12959.text: However, I myself would apply to God, And to God I would submit my cause,

12960.label: Job 5:9
12960.text: [To the] One doing great things unsearchable, Wonderful things without number;

12961.label: Job 5:10
12961.text: [To] the One giving rain upon the surface of the earth And sending waters upon the open fields;

12962.label: Job 5:11
12962.text: [To] the One putting those who are low on a high place, So that those who are sad are high up in salvation;

12963.label: Job 5:12
12963.text: [To the] One frustrating the schemes of the shrewd, So that their hands do not work with effect;

12964.label: Job 5:13
12964.text: [To the] One catching the wise in their own cunning, So that the counsel of astute ones is carried headlong;

12965.label: Job 5:14
12965.text: They encounter darkness even by day,And they grope about at midday as if at night;

12966.label: Job 5:15
12966.text: And [to the] One saving from the sword out of their mouth,And from the hand of the strong one, a poor one,

12967.label: Job 5:16
12967.text: So that for the lowly one there comes to be hope, But unrighteousness actually shuts its mouth.

12968.label: Job 5:17
12968.text: Look! Happy is the man whom God reproves; And the discipline of the Almighty do not you reject!

12969.label: Job 5:18
12969.text: For he himself causes pain, but binds up [the wound];He breaks to pieces, but his own hands do the healing.

12970.label: Job 5:19
12970.text: In six distresses he will deliver you, And in seven nothing injurious will touch you.

12971.label: Job 5:20
12971.text: During famine he will certainly redeem you from death, And during war from the power of a sword.

12972.label: Job 5:21
12972.text: From the whip of a tongue you will be hidden, And you will not be afraid of despoiling when it comes.

12973.label: Job 5:22
12973.text: At despoiling and hunger you will laugh,And of the wild beast of the earth you need not be afraid.

12974.label: Job 5:23
12974.text: For with the stones of the field your covenant will be,And the wild beast of the field himself will be made to live at peace with you.

12975.label: Job 5:24
12975.text: And you will certainly know that peace itself is your tent,And you will be bound to go and see your pasture ground, and you will miss nothing.

12976.label: Job 5:25
12976.text: And you will certainly know that your offspring are many And your descendants like the vegetation of the earth.

12977.label: Job 5:26
12977.text: You will come in vigor to the burial place, As when sheaves pile up in their time.

12978.label: Job 5:27
12978.text: Look! This is what we have investigated. So is it.Hear it, and you—know it for yourself.”

12979.label: Job 6:1
12979.text: And Job proceeded to answer and say:

12980.label: Job 6:2
12980.text: “O that my vexation were altogether weighed,And that at the same time my adversity they would put on scales themselves!

12981.label: Job 6:3
12981.text: For now it is heavier even than the sands of the seas.That is why my own words have been wild talk.

12982.label: Job 6:4
12982.text: For the arrows of the Almighty are with me, The venom of which my spirit is drinking; The terrors from God range themselves up against me.

12983.label: Job 6:5
12983.text: Will a zebra cry out over grass,Or a bull low over its fodder?

12984.label: Job 6:6
12984.text: Will tasteless things be eaten without salt,Or is there any taste in the slimy juice of marshmallow?

12985.label: Job 6:7
12985.text: My soul has refused to touch [anything].They are like disease in my food.

12986.label: Job 6:8
12986.text: O that my request would comeAnd that God would grant even my hope!

12987.label: Job 6:9
12987.text: And that God would go ahead and crush me,That he would release his hand and cut me off!

12988.label: Job 6:10
12988.text: Even it would still be my comfort;And I should leap [for joy] at [my] labor pains,[Though] he would have no compassion, for I have not hidden the sayings of the Holy One.

12989.label: Job 6:11
12989.text: What is my power, that I should keep waiting? And what is my end, that I should keep prolonging my soul?

12990.label: Job 6:12
12990.text: Is my power the power of stones?Or is my flesh of copper?

12991.label: Job 6:13
12991.text: Is it that self-assistance is not in me,And effectual working itself has been chased away from me?

12992.label: Job 6:14
12992.text: As regards anyone who withholds loving-kindness from his own fellow, He will also leave off even the fear of the Almighty.

12993.label: Job 6:15
12993.text: My own brothers have dealt treacherously, like a winter torrent,Like the channel of winter torrents that keep passing away.

12994.label: Job 6:16
12994.text: They are dark from ice,Upon them snow hides itself.

12995.label: Job 6:17
12995.text: In due season they become waterless, they have been silenced;When it grows hot they are dried up from their place.

12996.label: Job 6:18
12996.text: The paths of their way are turned aside;They go up into the empty place and perish.

12997.label: Job 6:19
12997.text: The caravans of Teʹma have looked,The traveling company of Sa·beʹans have waited for them.

12998.label: Job 6:20
12998.text: They certainly are ashamed because they had trusted;They have come clear to the place and they get disappointed.

12999.label: Job 6:21
12999.text: For now YOU men have amounted to nothing; YOU see terror, and YOU become afraid.

13000.label: Job 6:22
13000.text: Is it because I have said, ‘GIVE me [something],Or from some of the power of YOU men make a present in my behalf;

13001.label: Job 6:23
13001.text: And rescue me out of the hand of an adversary, And out of the hand of tyrants YOU men should redeem me’?

13002.label: Job 6:24
13002.text: Instruct me, and I, for my part, shall be silent; And what mistake I have committed make me understand.

13003.label: Job 6:25
13003.text: The sayings of uprightness have been—O not painful! But what does reproving on the part of YOU men reprove?

13004.label: Job 6:26
13004.text: Is it to reprove words that YOU men scheme,When the sayings of one in despair are for mere wind?

13005.label: Job 6:27
13005.text: How much more will YOU cast lots even over someone fatherless, And barter over YOUR companion!

13006.label: Job 6:28
13006.text: And now GO ahead, pay attention to me,[And see] whether I shall lie to YOUR very faces.

13007.label: Job 6:29
13007.text: Return, please—let no unrighteousness arise—Yes, return—my righteousness is yet in it.

13008.label: Job 6:30
13008.text: Is there unrighteousness on my tongue,Or does my own palate not discern adversity?

13009.label: Job 7:1
13009.text: “Is there not a compulsory labor for mortal man on earth,And are not his days like the days of a hired laborer?

13010.label: Job 7:2
13010.text: Like a slave he pants for the shadow, And like a hired laborer he waits for his wages.

13011.label: Job 7:3
13011.text: Thus I have been made to possess worthless lunar months, And nights of trouble they have counted out to me.

13012.label: Job 7:4
13012.text: When I have lain down I have also said, ‘When shall I get up?’ And [when] evening actually goes its measure, I have also been glutted with restlessness until morning twilight.

13013.label: Job 7:5
13013.text: My flesh has become clothed with maggots and lumps of dust; My skin itself has formed crusts and dissolves.

13014.label: Job 7:6
13014.text: My days themselves have become swifter than a weaver’s shuttle,And they come to an end in hopelessness.

13015.label: Job 7:7
13015.text: Remember that my life is wind; That my eye will not see good again.

13016.label: Job 7:8
13016.text: The eye of him that sees me will not behold me;Your eyes will be upon me, but I shall not be.

13017.label: Job 7:9
13017.text: The cloud certainly comes to its end and goes away;So he that is going down to Sheʹol will not come up.

13018.label: Job 7:10
13018.text: He will not return anymore to his house,And his place will not acknowledge him anymore.

13019.label: Job 7:11
13019.text: I, also, I shall not hold back my mouth.I will speak in the distress of my spirit; I will be concerned with the bitterness of my soul!

13020.label: Job 7:12
13020.text: Am I a sea or a sea monster,That you should set a guard over me?

13021.label: Job 7:13
13021.text: When I said, ‘My divan will comfort me,My bed will help carry my concern,’

13022.label: Job 7:14
13022.text: You even have terrified me with dreams,And by visions you make me start up in fright,

13023.label: Job 7:15
13023.text: So that my soul chooses suffocation,Death rather than my bones.

13024.label: Job 7:16
13024.text: I have rejected [it]; to time indefinite I would not live.Cease from me, for my days are an exhalation.

13025.label: Job 7:17
13025.text: What is mortal man that you should rear him, And that you should set your heart upon him,

13026.label: Job 7:18
13026.text: And that you should pay attention to him every morning,That every moment you should test him?

13027.label: Job 7:19
13027.text: Why will you not turn your gaze from me, Nor let me alone until I swallow my saliva?

13028.label: Job 7:20
13028.text: If I have sinned, what can I accomplish against you, the Observer of mankind? Why is it that you have set me as your target, so that I should become a burden to you?

13029.label: Job 7:21
13029.text: And why do you not pardon my transgression And overlook my error?For now in dust I shall lie down;And you will certainly look for me, and I shall not be.”

13030.label: Job 8:1
13030.text: And Bilʹdad the Shuʹhite proceeded to answer and say:

13031.label: Job 8:2
13031.text: “How long will you keep uttering these things, When the sayings of your mouth are but a powerful wind?

13032.label: Job 8:3
13032.text: Will God himself pervert judgment, Or will the Almighty himself pervert righteousness?

13033.label: Job 8:4
13033.text: If your own sons have sinned against him,So that he lets them go into the hand of their revolt,

13034.label: Job 8:5
13034.text: If you yourself will look for God, And [if] of the Almighty you will implore favor,

13035.label: Job 8:6
13035.text: If you are pure and upright, By now he would awake for you And he would certainly restore your righteous abiding place.

13036.label: Job 8:7
13036.text: Also, your beginning may have proved to be a small thing,But your own end afterward would grow very great.

13037.label: Job 8:8
13037.text: Indeed, ask, please, of the former generation, And direct [your attention] to the things searched out by their fathers.

13038.label: Job 8:9
13038.text: For we were only yesterday, and we know nothing,Because our days on earth are a shadow.

13039.label: Job 8:10
13039.text: Will not they themselves instruct you, tell you, And from their heart will they not bring forth words?

13040.label: Job 8:11
13040.text: Will a papyrus plant grow tall without a swampy place?Will a reed grow big without water?

13041.label: Job 8:12
13041.text: While it is yet in its bud, not plucked off,Even ahead of all other grass it will dry up.

13042.label: Job 8:13
13042.text: Thus are the pathways of all those forgetting God, And the very hope of an apostate will perish,

13043.label: Job 8:14
13043.text: Whose confidence is cut off,And whose trust is a spider’s house.

13044.label: Job 8:15
13044.text: He will lean upon his house, but it will not keep standing;He will take hold of it, but it will not last.

13045.label: Job 8:16
13045.text: He is full of sap before the sun,And in his garden his own twig goes forth.

13046.label: Job 8:17
13046.text: In a stone heap his roots become interwoven,A house of stones he beholds.

13047.label: Job 8:18
13047.text: If one swallows him up from his place, It will also certainly deny him, [saying,] ‘I have not seen you.’

13048.label: Job 8:19
13048.text: Look! That is the dissolving of his way; And from the dust others spring up.

13049.label: Job 8:20
13049.text: Look! God himself will not reject anyone blameless,Neither will he take hold of the hand of evildoers,

13050.label: Job 8:21
13050.text: Until he fills your mouth with laughter,And your lips with joyful shouting.

13051.label: Job 8:22
13051.text: The very ones hating you will be clothed with shame, And the tent of wicked ones will not be.”

13052.label: Job 9:1
13052.text: And Job proceeded to answer and say:

13053.label: Job 9:2
13053.text: “For a fact I do know that it is so.But how can mortal man be in the right in a case with God?

13054.label: Job 9:3
13054.text: If he should find delight in contending with him, He cannot answer him once out of a thousand.

13055.label: Job 9:4
13055.text: He is wise in heart and strong in power. Who can show stubbornness to him and come off uninjured?

13056.label: Job 9:5
13056.text: He is moving mountains away, so that people do not even know [of them],He who has overthrown them in his anger.

13057.label: Job 9:6
13057.text: He is making the earth go quaking from its place,So that its very pillars shudder.

13058.label: Job 9:7
13058.text: He is saying to the sun that it should not shine forth,And around stars he puts a seal,

13059.label: Job 9:8
13059.text: Stretching out the heavens by himself And treading upon the high waves of the sea;

13060.label: Job 9:9
13060.text: Making the Ash constellation, the Keʹsil constellation, And the Kiʹmah constellation and the interior rooms of the South;

13061.label: Job 9:10
13061.text: Doing great things unsearchable, And wonderful things without number.

13062.label: Job 9:11
13062.text: Look! He passes by me and I do not see [him],And he moves on and I do not discern him.

13063.label: Job 9:12
13063.text: Look! He snatches away. Who can resist him?Who will say to him, ‘What are you doing?’

13064.label: Job 9:13
13064.text: God himself will not turn back his anger; Beneath him the helpers of a stormer must bow down.

13065.label: Job 9:14
13065.text: How much more so in case I myself answer him!I will choose my words with him,

13066.label: Job 9:15
13066.text: Whom I would not answer, even though I were really in the right. Of my opponent-at-law I would implore favor.

13067.label: Job 9:16
13067.text: If I called him, would he answer me? I do not believe that he would give ear to my voice;

13068.label: Job 9:17
13068.text: Who with a storm bruises meAnd certainly makes my wounds many for no reason.

13069.label: Job 9:18
13069.text: He will not grant me my taking of a fresh breath, For he keeps glutting me with bitter things.

13070.label: Job 9:19
13070.text: If in power anyone is strong, there [he is]; And if in justice [anyone is strong], O that I may be summoned!

13071.label: Job 9:20
13071.text: If I were in the right, my own mouth would pronounce me wicked;Were I blameless, then he would declare me crooked.

13072.label: Job 9:21
13072.text: Were I blameless, I would not know my soul;I would refuse my life.

13073.label: Job 9:22
13073.text: One thing there is. That is why I do say,‘One blameless, also a wicked one, he is bringing to their end.’

13074.label: Job 9:23
13074.text: If a flash flood itself should cause death suddenly,At the very despair of the innocent ones he would mock.

13075.label: Job 9:24
13075.text: Earth itself has been given into the hand of the wicked one; The face of its judges he covers.If not, who, then, is it?

13076.label: Job 9:25
13076.text: Also my own days have become swifter than a runner; They have run away, they will certainly not see good.

13077.label: Job 9:26
13077.text: They have moved on like reed boats,Like an eagle that darts to and fro for something to eat.

13078.label: Job 9:27
13078.text: If I have said, ‘Let me forget my concern, Let me alter my countenance and brighten up,’

13079.label: Job 9:28
13079.text: I have been scared of all my pains; I do know that you will not hold me innocent.

13080.label: Job 9:29
13080.text: I myself am to become wicked.Why is it that I toil merely in vain?

13081.label: Job 9:30
13081.text: If I actually washed myself in snow water,And I actually cleansed my hands in potash,

13082.label: Job 9:31
13082.text: Then in a pit you would dip me,And my garments would certainly detest me.

13083.label: Job 9:32
13083.text: For he is not a man like me [that] I should answer him,That we should come together in judgment.

13084.label: Job 9:33
13084.text: There exists no person to decide between us, That he should put his hand upon both of us.

13085.label: Job 9:34
13085.text: Let him remove his rod from upon me, And his frightfulness, let it not terrify me.

13086.label: Job 9:35
13086.text: Let me speak and not be afraid of him,For I am not so disposed in myself.

13087.label: Job 10:1
13087.text: “My soul certainly feels a loathing toward my life. I will give vent to my concern about myself. I will speak in the bitterness of my soul!

13088.label: Job 10:2
13088.text: I shall say to God, ‘Do not pronounce me wicked.Cause me to know why it is that you are contending with me.

13089.label: Job 10:3
13089.text: Is it good for you that you should do wrong, That you should reject [the product of] the hard work of your hands, And that upon the counsel of wicked ones you should actually beam?

13090.label: Job 10:4
13090.text: Do you have eyes of flesh,Or is it as a mortal man sees that you see?

13091.label: Job 10:5
13091.text: Are your days like the days of mortal man, Or your years just like the days of an able-bodied man,

13092.label: Job 10:6
13092.text: That you should try to find my errorAnd for my sin you should keep looking?

13093.label: Job 10:7
13093.text: This in spite of your own knowledge that I am not in the wrong, And there is no one delivering out of your own hand?

13094.label: Job 10:8
13094.text: Your own hands have shaped me so that they made me In entirety round about, and yet you would swallow me up.

13095.label: Job 10:9
13095.text: Remember, please, that out of clay you have made meAnd to dust you will make me return.

13096.label: Job 10:10
13096.text: Did you not proceed to pour me out as milk itselfAnd like cheese to curdle me?

13097.label: Job 10:11
13097.text: With skin and flesh you proceeded to clothe meAnd with bones and sinews to weave me together.

13098.label: Job 10:12
13098.text: Life and loving-kindness you have worked with me; And your own care has guarded my spirit.

13099.label: Job 10:13
13099.text: And these things you have concealed in your heart.I well know that these things are with you.

13100.label: Job 10:14
13100.text: If I have sinned and you have kept watching meAnd of my error you do not hold me innocent;

13101.label: Job 10:15
13101.text: If I am actually in the wrong, too bad for me! And [if] I am actually in the right, I may not raise my head, Glutted with dishonor and saturated with affliction.

13102.label: Job 10:16
13102.text: And [if] it acts haughtily, like a young lion you will hunt for me, And you will again show yourself marvelous in my case.

13103.label: Job 10:17
13103.text: You will bring forth new witnesses of yours in front of me,And you will make your vexation with me greater;Hardship after hardship is with me.

13104.label: Job 10:18
13104.text: So why from a womb did you bring me out? Could I have expired, that not even an eye could see me,

13105.label: Job 10:19
13105.text: There as though I had not come to be I should have become;From the belly to the burial place I should have been brought.’

13106.label: Job 10:20
13106.text: Are not my days few? Let him leave off,Let him turn his gaze from me, that I may brighten up a little

13107.label: Job 10:21
13107.text: Before I go away—and I shall not come back —To the land of darkness and deep shadow,

13108.label: Job 10:22
13108.text: To the land of obscurity like gloom, of deep shadowAnd disorder, where it beams no more than gloom does.”

13109.label: Job 11:1
13109.text: And Zoʹphar the Naʹa·ma·thite proceeded to answer and say:

13110.label: Job 11:2
13110.text: “Will a multitude of words go unanswered,Or will a mere boaster be in the right?

13111.label: Job 11:3
13111.text: Will your empty talk itself put men to silence,And will you keep deriding without having anyone rebuke [you]?

13112.label: Job 11:4
13112.text: Also, you say, ‘My instruction is pure,And I have proved really clean in your eyes.’

13113.label: Job 11:5
13113.text: Yet O if only God himself would speakAnd open his lips with you!

13114.label: Job 11:6
13114.text: Then he would tell you the secrets of wisdom,For the things of practical wisdom are manifold. Also, you would know that God allows some of your error to be forgotten for you.

13115.label: Job 11:7
13115.text: Can you find out the deep things of God, Or can you find out to the very limit of the Almighty?

13116.label: Job 11:8
13116.text: It is higher than heaven. What can you accomplish?It is deeper than Sheʹol. What can you know?

13117.label: Job 11:9
13117.text: It is longer than the earth in measure,And broader than the sea.

13118.label: Job 11:10
13118.text: If he moves on and hands [someone] overAnd calls a court, then who can resist him?

13119.label: Job 11:11
13119.text: For he himself well knows men who are untrue. When he sees what is hurtful, will he not also show himself attentive?

13120.label: Job 11:12
13120.text: Even a hollow-minded man himself will get good motiveAs soon as an asinine zebra be born a man.

13121.label: Job 11:13
13121.text: If you yourself will really prepare your heartAnd actually spread out your palms to him,

13122.label: Job 11:14
13122.text: If what is hurtful is in your hand, put it far away,And let no unrighteousness dwell in your tents.

13123.label: Job 11:15
13123.text: For then you will raise your face without defect And you will certainly become established, and you will not fear.

13124.label: Job 11:16
13124.text: For you—you will forget trouble itself;As waters that have passed along you will remember [it].

13125.label: Job 11:17
13125.text: And brighter than midday will [your] life’s duration arise;Darkness will become like the morning itself.

13126.label: Job 11:18
13126.text: And you will be bound to trust because there exists hope;And you will certainly look carefully around—in security you will lie down.

13127.label: Job 11:19
13127.text: And you will indeed stretch yourself out, with no one to make [you] tremble.And many people will certainly put you in a gentle mood;

13128.label: Job 11:20
13128.text: And the very eyes of the wicked will fail; And a place for flight will certainly perish from them, And their hope will be an expiring of the soul.”

13129.label: Job 12:1
13129.text: And Job proceeded to answer and say:

13130.label: Job 12:2
13130.text: “For a fact YOU men are the people,And with YOU wisdom will die out!

13131.label: Job 12:3
13131.text: I too have a heart as well as YOU.I am not inferior to YOU, And with whom are there not things like these?

13132.label: Job 12:4
13132.text: [One who is] a laughingstock to his fellowman I become, One calling to God that he should answer him. A laughingstock is the righteous, unblamable one.

13133.label: Job 12:5
13133.text: In thought, the carefree one has contempt for extinction itself; It is made ready for those of wobbling feet.

13134.label: Job 12:6
13134.text: The tents of the despoilers are unworried, And the ones enraging God have the safetyBelonging to one who has brought a god in his hand.

13135.label: Job 12:7
13135.text: However, ask, please, the domestic animals, and they will instruct you; Also the winged creatures of the heavens, and they will tell you.

13136.label: Job 12:8
13136.text: Or show your concern to the earth, and it will instruct you; And the fishes of the sea will declare it to you.

13137.label: Job 12:9
13137.text: Who among all these does not well knowThat the hand of Jehovah itself has done this,

13138.label: Job 12:10
13138.text: In whose hand is the soul of everyone aliveAnd the spirit of all flesh of man?

13139.label: Job 12:11
13139.text: Does not the ear itself test out words As the palate tastes food?

13140.label: Job 12:12
13140.text: Is there not wisdom among the aged And understanding [in] length of days?

13141.label: Job 12:13
13141.text: With him there are wisdom and mightiness; He has counsel and understanding.

13142.label: Job 12:14
13142.text: Look! He tears down, that there may be no building up; He makes it shut to man, that it may not be opened up.

13143.label: Job 12:15
13143.text: Look! He puts a restraint upon the waters and they dry up; And he sends them, and they change the earth.

13144.label: Job 12:16
13144.text: With him there are strength and practical wisdom; To him belong the one making a mistake and the one leading astray;

13145.label: Job 12:17
13145.text: He is making counselors go barefoot, And he makes judges themselves go crazy.

13146.label: Job 12:18
13146.text: The bonds of kings he actually loosens, And he binds a belt upon their hips.

13147.label: Job 12:19
13147.text: He is making priests walk barefoot, And permanently seated ones he subverts;

13148.label: Job 12:20
13148.text: He is removing speech from the faithful ones,And the sensibleness of old men he takes away;

13149.label: Job 12:21
13149.text: He is pouring out contempt upon nobles, And the girdle of powerful ones he actually weakens;

13150.label: Job 12:22
13150.text: He is uncovering deep things from the darkness, And he brings forth to the light deep shadow;

13151.label: Job 12:23
13151.text: Making the nations grow great, that he may destroy them; Spreading out the nations, that he may lead them away;

13152.label: Job 12:24
13152.text: Taking away the heart of the head ones of the people of the land,That he may make them wander about in an empty place, where there is no way.

13153.label: Job 12:25
13153.text: They grope in darkness, where there is no light,That he may make them wander about like a drunken man.

13154.label: Job 13:1
13154.text: “Look! All this my eye has seen,My ear has heard and considers it.

13155.label: Job 13:2
13155.text: What YOU men know I myself well know also;I am not inferior to YOU.

13156.label: Job 13:3
13156.text: However, I, for my part, would speak to the Almighty himself, And in arguing with God I would find delight.

13157.label: Job 13:4
13157.text: On the other hand, YOU men are smearers of falsehood; All of YOU are physicians of no value.

13158.label: Job 13:5
13158.text: If only YOU would absolutely keep silent,That it might prove to be wisdom on YOUR part!

13159.label: Job 13:6
13159.text: Hear, please, my counterarguments, And to the pleadings of my lips pay attention.

13160.label: Job 13:7
13160.text: Will YOU men speak unrighteousness for God himself,And for him will YOU speak deceit?

13161.label: Job 13:8
13161.text: Will YOU be treating him with partiality, Or for the [true] God will YOU contend at law?

13162.label: Job 13:9
13162.text: Would it be good that he sound YOU out? Or as one trifles with mortal man will YOU trifle with him?

13163.label: Job 13:10
13163.text: He will positively reprove YOU If in secrecy YOU try to show partiality;

13164.label: Job 13:11
13164.text: Will not his very dignity make YOU start up with fright,And the very dread of him fall upon YOU?

13165.label: Job 13:12
13165.text: YOUR memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes;YOUR shield bosses are as shield bosses of clay.

13166.label: Job 13:13
13166.text: KEEP silent before me, that I myself may speak.Then let come upon me whatever it may be!

13167.label: Job 13:14
13167.text: Why do I carry my flesh in my teethAnd place my own soul in my palm?

13168.label: Job 13:15
13168.text: Even if he would slay me, would I not wait? I would only argue to his face for my own ways.

13169.label: Job 13:16
13169.text: He would also be my salvation, For before him no apostate will come in.

13170.label: Job 13:17
13170.text: HEAR my word clear through, And let my declaration be in YOUR ears.

13171.label: Job 13:18
13171.text: Look! Please, I have presented a case of justice; I well know that I myself am in the right.

13172.label: Job 13:19
13172.text: Who is the one that will contend with me? For now were I to become silent I should simply expire!

13173.label: Job 13:20
13173.text: Only two things do not do to me;In that case I shall not conceal myself just on your account;

13174.label: Job 13:21
13174.text: Put your own hand far away from upon me,And the fright of you—may it not terrify me.

13175.label: Job 13:22
13175.text: Either call that I myself may answer;Or may I speak, and you return me answer.

13176.label: Job 13:23
13176.text: In what way do I have errors and sins?Make me to know my own revolt and my own sin.

13177.label: Job 13:24
13177.text: Why do you conceal your very face And regard me as an enemy of yours?

13178.label: Job 13:25
13178.text: Will you make a mere leaf driven about quiver,Or keep chasing after mere dry stubble?

13179.label: Job 13:26
13179.text: For you keep writing against me bitter things And you make me possess [the consequences of] the errors of my youth.

13180.label: Job 13:27
13180.text: You also keep my feet put in the stocks, And you watch all my paths;For the soles of my feet you mark your own line.

13181.label: Job 13:28
13181.text: And he is like something rotten that wears out; Like a garment that a moth actually eats up.

13182.label: Job 14:1
13182.text: “Man, born of woman, Is short-lived and glutted with agitation.

13183.label: Job 14:2
13183.text: Like a blossom he has come forth and is cut off, And he runs away like the shadow and does not keep existing.

13184.label: Job 14:3
13184.text: Yes, upon this one you have opened your eye,And me you bring into judgment with you.

13185.label: Job 14:4
13185.text: Who can produce someone clean out of someone unclean? There is not one.

13186.label: Job 14:5
13186.text: If his days are decided, The number of his months is with you;A decree for him you have made that he may not go beyond.

13187.label: Job 14:6
13187.text: Turn your gaze from upon him that he may have rest, Until he finds pleasure as a hired laborer does in his day.

13188.label: Job 14:7
13188.text: For there exists hope for even a tree.If it gets cut down, it will even sprout again, And its own twig will not cease to be.

13189.label: Job 14:8
13189.text: If its root grows old in the earthAnd in the dust its stump dies,

13190.label: Job 14:9
13190.text: At the scent of water it will sprout And it will certainly produce a bough like a new plant.

13191.label: Job 14:10
13191.text: But an able-bodied man dies and lies vanquished;And an earthling man expires, and where is he?

13192.label: Job 14:11
13192.text: Waters do disappear from a sea,And a river itself drains off and dries up.

13193.label: Job 14:12
13193.text: Man also has to lie down and does not get up. Until heaven is no more they will not wake up, Nor will they be aroused from their sleep.

13194.label: Job 14:13
13194.text: O that in Sheʹol you would conceal me, That you would keep me secret until your anger turns back,That you would set a time limit for me and remember me!

13195.label: Job 14:14
13195.text: If an able-bodied man dies can he live again? All the days of my compulsory service I shall wait, Until my relief comes.

13196.label: Job 14:15
13196.text: You will call, and I myself shall answer you. For the work of your hands you will have a yearning.

13197.label: Job 14:16
13197.text: For now you keep counting my very steps; You watch for nothing but my sin.

13198.label: Job 14:17
13198.text: Sealed up in a bag is my revolt, And you apply glue over my error.

13199.label: Job 14:18
13199.text: However, a mountain itself, falling, will fade away,And even a rock will be moved away from its place.

13200.label: Job 14:19
13200.text: Water certainly rubs away even stones;Its outpouring washes off earth’s dust.So you have destroyed the very hope of mortal man.

13201.label: Job 14:20
13201.text: You overpower him forever so that he goes away; You are disfiguring his face so that you send him away.

13202.label: Job 14:21
13202.text: His sons get honored, but he does not know [it]; And they become insignificant, but he does not consider them.

13203.label: Job 14:22
13203.text: Only his own flesh while upon him will keep aching,And his own soul while within him will keep mourning.”

13204.label: Job 15:1
13204.text: And Elʹi·phaz the Teʹman·ite proceeded to answer and say:

13205.label: Job 15:2
13205.text: “Will a wise person himself answer with windy knowledge, Or will he fill his belly with the east wind?

13206.label: Job 15:3
13206.text: Merely reproving with a word will be of no use,And mere utterances will be of no benefit by themselves.

13207.label: Job 15:4
13207.text: However, you yourself make fear [before God] to have no force,And you diminish the having of any concern before God.

13208.label: Job 15:5
13208.text: For your error trains your mouth, And you choose the tongue of shrewd people.

13209.label: Job 15:6
13209.text: Your mouth pronounces you wicked, and not I;And your own lips answer against you.

13210.label: Job 15:7
13210.text: Were you the very first man to be born, Or before the hills were you brought forth with labor pains?

13211.label: Job 15:8
13211.text: To the confidential talk of God do you listen, And do you limit wisdom to yourself?

13212.label: Job 15:9
13212.text: What do you actually know that we do not know? What do you understand that is not also with us?

13213.label: Job 15:10
13213.text: Both the gray-headed and the aged one are with us, The one greater than your father in days.

13214.label: Job 15:11
13214.text: Are the consolations of God not enough for you,Or a word [spoken] gently with you?

13215.label: Job 15:12
13215.text: Why does your heart carry you away,And why do your eyes flash?

13216.label: Job 15:13
13216.text: For you turn your spirit against God himself,And you have caused words to go forth from your own mouth.

13217.label: Job 15:14
13217.text: What is mortal man that he should be clean, Or that anyone born of a woman should be in the right?

13218.label: Job 15:15
13218.text: Look! In his holy ones he has no faith, And the heavens themselves are actually not clean in his eyes.

13219.label: Job 15:16
13219.text: How much less so when one is detestable and corrupt, A man who is drinking in unrighteousness just like water!

13220.label: Job 15:17
13220.text: I shall declare it to you. Listen to me! Even this I have beheld, so let me relate [it],

13221.label: Job 15:18
13221.text: That which wise ones themselves tellAnd which they did not hide, [it being] from their fathers.

13222.label: Job 15:19
13222.text: To them alone the land was given,And no stranger passed through the midst of them.

13223.label: Job 15:20
13223.text: All his days a wicked one is suffering torture,Even the very number of years that have been reserved for the tyrant.

13224.label: Job 15:21
13224.text: The sound of dreadful things is in his ears;During peace a despoiler himself comes upon him.

13225.label: Job 15:22
13225.text: He does not believe that he will come back out of darkness, And he is reserved for a sword.

13226.label: Job 15:23
13226.text: He is straying about in search of bread —where is it? He well knows that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.

13227.label: Job 15:24
13227.text: Distress and anguish keep terrifying him; They overpower him like a king in readiness for the assault.

13228.label: Job 15:25
13228.text: Because he stretches out his hand against God himself,And over the Almighty he tries to show himself superior;

13229.label: Job 15:26
13229.text: [Because] he runs against him stiff-neckedly,With the thick bosses of his shields;

13230.label: Job 15:27
13230.text: Because he actually covers his face with his fattinessAnd he puts on fat upon his loins,

13231.label: Job 15:28
13231.text: He merely resides in cities that are to be effaced;In houses in which people will not keep dwelling,Which certainly prove destined for heaps of stones.

13232.label: Job 15:29
13232.text: He will not grow rich and his wealth will not mount up,Nor will he spread out the acquisition of them over the earth.

13233.label: Job 15:30
13233.text: He will not turn away from darkness;His twig a flame will dry up,And he will turn aside by a blast of His mouth.

13234.label: Job 15:31
13234.text: Let him put no faith in worthlessness, being led astray,For mere worthlessness will prove to be what he gets in exchange;

13235.label: Job 15:32
13235.text: Before his day will it be fulfilled.And his shoot itself will certainly not grow luxuriantly.

13236.label: Job 15:33
13236.text: He will thrust away his unripe grapes just like a vine,And cast off his blossoms just like an olive tree.

13237.label: Job 15:34
13237.text: For the assembly of apostates is sterile, And fire itself must eat up the tents of bribery.

13238.label: Job 15:35
13238.text: There is a conceiving of trouble and a giving birth to what is hurtful, And their belly itself prepares deceit.”

13239.label: Job 16:1
13239.text: And Job proceeded to answer and say:

13240.label: Job 16:2
13240.text: “I have heard many things like these.All of YOU are troublesome comforters!

13241.label: Job 16:3
13241.text: Is there an end to windy words? Or what galls you, that you answer?

13242.label: Job 16:4
13242.text: I myself also could well speak as YOU men do.If only YOUR souls existed where my soul is,Would I be brilliant in words against YOU, And would I wag my head against YOU?

13243.label: Job 16:5
13243.text: I would strengthen YOU with the words of my mouth, And the consolation of my own lips would hold back—.

13244.label: Job 16:6
13244.text: If I do speak, my own pain is not held back, And if I do cease doing so, what goes away from me?

13245.label: Job 16:7
13245.text: Only now he has made me weary; He has made all those assembling with me desolate.

13246.label: Job 16:8
13246.text: You also seize me. It has become a witness, So that my leanness rises up against me. In my face it testifies.

13247.label: Job 16:9
13247.text: His very anger has torn [me] to pieces, and he harbors animosity against me.He actually grinds his teeth against me. My adversary himself sharpens his eyes against me.

13248.label: Job 16:10
13248.text: They have opened their mouth wide against me, With reproach they have struck my cheeks,In large number they mass themselves against me.

13249.label: Job 16:11
13249.text: God hands me over to young boys, And into the hands of wicked ones he throws me headlong.

13250.label: Job 16:12
13250.text: I had come to be at ease, but he proceeded to shake me up; And he grabbed me by the back of the neck and proceeded to smash me,And he sets me up as a target for himself.

13251.label: Job 16:13
13251.text: His archers encircle me;He splits open my kidneys and feels no compassion;He pours out my gallbladder to the very earth.

13252.label: Job 16:14
13252.text: He keeps breaking through me with breach after breach;He runs at me like a mighty one.

13253.label: Job 16:15
13253.text: Sackcloth I have sewed together over my skin,And I have thrust my horn in the very dust.

13254.label: Job 16:16
13254.text: My face itself has become reddened from weeping, And upon my eyelids there is deep shadow,

13255.label: Job 16:17
13255.text: Although there is no violence upon my palms,And my prayer is pure.

13256.label: Job 16:18
13256.text: O earth, do not cover my blood! And let there prove to be no place for my outcry!

13257.label: Job 16:19
13257.text: Also now, look! in the heavens is one testifying about me,And my witness is in the heights.

13258.label: Job 16:20
13258.text: My companions are spokesmen against me; To God my eye has looked sleeplessly.

13259.label: Job 16:21
13259.text: And the decision is to be made between an able-bodied man and God,The same as between a son of man and his fellow.

13260.label: Job 16:22
13260.text: For just a few years are to come,And by the path by which I shall not return I shall go away.

13261.label: Job 17:1
13261.text: “My very spirit has been broken, my own days have been extinguished;The graveyard is for me.

13262.label: Job 17:2
13262.text: Certainly there is mockery at me, And amid their rebellious behavior my eye lodges.

13263.label: Job 17:3
13263.text: Please, do put my security with yourself. Who else is there that will shake hands with me in pledge?

13264.label: Job 17:4
13264.text: For their heart you have closed to discretion. That is why you do not exalt them.

13265.label: Job 17:5
13265.text: He may tell companions to take their shares,But the very eyes of his sons will fail.

13266.label: Job 17:6
13266.text: And he has set me forth as a proverbial saying of peoples,So that I become someone into whose face to spit.

13267.label: Job 17:7
13267.text: And from vexation my eye grows dimmer And my members are all of them like the shadow.

13268.label: Job 17:8
13268.text: Upright people stare in amazement at this,And even the innocent one gets excited over the apostate.

13269.label: Job 17:9
13269.text: The righteous one keeps holding fast to his way, And the one with clean hands keeps increasing in strength.

13270.label: Job 17:10
13270.text: However, YOU men may all of YOU resume. So come on, please,As I do not find anyone wise among YOU.

13271.label: Job 17:11
13271.text: My own days have passed along, my own plans have been torn apart, The wishes of my heart.

13272.label: Job 17:12
13272.text: Night they keep putting for day: ‘Light is near on account of darkness.’

13273.label: Job 17:13
13273.text: If I keep waiting, Sheʹol is my house; In the darkness I shall have to spread out my lounge.

13274.label: Job 17:14
13274.text: To the pit I shall have to call out, ‘You are my father!’To the maggot, ‘My mother and my sister!’

13275.label: Job 17:15
13275.text: So where, then, is my hope? And my hope—who is it that beholds it?

13276.label: Job 17:16
13276.text: To the bars of Sheʹol they will go down,When we, all together, must descend to the very dust.”

13277.label: Job 18:1
13277.text: And Bilʹdad the Shuʹhite proceeded to answer and say:

13278.label: Job 18:2
13278.text: “How long will YOU people be at putting an end to words?YOU should understand, that afterward we may speak.

13279.label: Job 18:3
13279.text: Why should we be reckoned as beasts [And] be regarded as unclean in YOUR eyes?

13280.label: Job 18:4
13280.text: He is tearing his soul to pieces in his anger.For your sake will the earth be abandoned,Or a rock move away from its place?

13281.label: Job 18:5
13281.text: The light also of wicked ones will be extinguished And the spark of his fire will not shine.

13282.label: Job 18:6
13282.text: A light itself will certainly grow dark in his tent, And in it his own lamp will be extinguished.

13283.label: Job 18:7
13283.text: His steps of vigor will become cramped.Even his counsel will cast him off.

13284.label: Job 18:8
13284.text: For he will indeed be let go into a net by his feet,And onto a network he will walk.

13285.label: Job 18:9
13285.text: A trap will seize [him] by the heel; A snare keeps hold upon him.

13286.label: Job 18:10
13286.text: A cord for him is hidden on the earth,And a catching device for him on [his] pathway.

13287.label: Job 18:11
13287.text: Round about, sudden terrors certainly make him start up in fright, And indeed chase him at his feet.

13288.label: Job 18:12
13288.text: His vigor becomes famished,And disaster stands ready to make him limp.

13289.label: Job 18:13
13289.text: It will eat the pieces of his skin; The firstborn of death will eat his limbs.

13290.label: Job 18:14
13290.text: His confidence will be torn away from his own tent And it will march him to the king of terrors.

13291.label: Job 18:15
13291.text: There will reside in his tent something that is not his;Sulphur will be strewed upon his own abiding place.

13292.label: Job 18:16
13292.text: Underneath will his very roots dry up, And, up above, his bough will wither.

13293.label: Job 18:17
13293.text: The very mentioning of him will certainly perish from the earth, And he will have no name out in the street.

13294.label: Job 18:18
13294.text: They will push him out of the light into the darkness,And from the productive land they will chase him away.

13295.label: Job 18:19
13295.text: He will have no posterity and no progeny among his people, And there will be no survivor in his place of alien residence.

13296.label: Job 18:20
13296.text: At his day the people in the West will indeed stare in amazement,And a shudder will certainly seize even the people in the East.

13297.label: Job 18:21
13297.text: Only these are the tabernacles of a wrongdoer,And this is the place of one that has not known God.”

13298.label: Job 19:1
13298.text: And Job proceeded to answer and say:

13299.label: Job 19:2
13299.text: “How long will YOU men keep irritating my soul And keep crushing me with words?

13300.label: Job 19:3
13300.text: These ten times YOU proceeded to rebuke me;YOU are not ashamed [that] YOU deal so hard with me.

13301.label: Job 19:4
13301.text: And, granted that I have made a mistake, It is with me that my mistake will lodge.

13302.label: Job 19:5
13302.text: If for a fact against me YOU men do put on great airs, And YOU show my reproach to be proper against me,

13303.label: Job 19:6
13303.text: KNOW, then, that God himself has misled me,And his hunting net he has closed in upon me.

13304.label: Job 19:7
13304.text: Look! I keep crying out, ‘Violence!’ but I get no answer; I keep crying for help, but there is no justice.

13305.label: Job 19:8
13305.text: My very path he has blocked with a stone wall, and I cannot pass over;And upon my roadways he puts darkness itself.

13306.label: Job 19:9
13306.text: My own glory he has stripped from me, And he takes away the crown of my head.

13307.label: Job 19:10
13307.text: He pulls me down on all sides, and I go away;And he pulls my hope out just like a tree.

13308.label: Job 19:11
13308.text: His anger also grows hot against me, And he keeps reckoning me as an adversary of his.

13309.label: Job 19:12
13309.text: Unitedly his troops come and cast up their way against me, And they camp round about my tent.

13310.label: Job 19:13
13310.text: My own brothers he has put far away from me, And the very ones knowing me have even turned aside from me.

13311.label: Job 19:14
13311.text: My intimate acquaintances have ceased to be, And those known by me have themselves forgotten me,

13312.label: Job 19:15
13312.text: Those residing as aliens in my house; and my slave girls themselves reckon me as a stranger;A real foreigner I have become in their eyes.

13313.label: Job 19:16
13313.text: To my servant I have called, but he does not answer.With my own mouth I keep imploring him for compassion.

13314.label: Job 19:17
13314.text: My breath itself has become loathsome to my wife, And I have become foul-smelling to the sons of my [mother’s] belly.

13315.label: Job 19:18
13315.text: Also young boys themselves have rejected me; Let me but rise up, and they begin to speak against me.

13316.label: Job 19:19
13316.text: All the men of my intimate group detest me, And those whom I loved have turned against me.

13317.label: Job 19:20
13317.text: To my skin and to my flesh my bones actually cleave, And I escape with the skin of my teeth.

13318.label: Job 19:21
13318.text: Show me some favor, show me some favor, O YOU my companions, For God’s own hand has touched me.

13319.label: Job 19:22
13319.text: Why do YOU men keep persecuting me as God does, And not become satisfied with my very flesh?

13320.label: Job 19:23
13320.text: O that now my words were written down!O that in a book they were even inscribed!

13321.label: Job 19:24
13321.text: With an iron stylus and [with] lead,Forever in the rock O that they were hewn!

13322.label: Job 19:25
13322.text: And I myself well know that my redeemer is alive,And that, coming after [me], he will rise up over [the] dust.

13323.label: Job 19:26
13323.text: And after my skin, [which] they have skinned off,—this!Yet reduced in my flesh I shall behold God,

13324.label: Job 19:27
13324.text: Whom even I shall behold for myself, And [whom] my very eyes will certainly see, but not some stranger.My kidneys have failed deep within me.

13325.label: Job 19:28
13325.text: For YOU men say, ‘Why do we keep persecuting him?’When the very root of [the] matter is found in me.

13326.label: Job 19:29
13326.text: Be frightened for yourselves because of a sword, For the sword means a raging against errors,In order that YOU men may know there is a judge.”

13327.label: Job 20:1
13327.text: And Zoʹphar the Naʹa·ma·thite proceeded to reply and say:

13328.label: Job 20:2
13328.text: “Therefore do my own disquieting thoughts themselves answer me,Even on account of my inward excitement.

13329.label: Job 20:3
13329.text: An insulting exhortation to me I hear;And a spirit without the understanding that I have replies to me.

13330.label: Job 20:4
13330.text: Have you at all times known this very thing,Since man was put upon the earth,

13331.label: Job 20:5
13331.text: That the joyful cry of wicked people is short And the rejoicing of an apostate is for a moment?

13332.label: Job 20:6
13332.text: Although his excellency ascends to heaven itself And his very head reaches to the clouds,

13333.label: Job 20:7
13333.text: Like his manure cakes he perishes forever; The very ones seeing him will say, ‘Where is he?’

13334.label: Job 20:8
13334.text: Like a dream he will fly off, and they will not find him;And he will be chased away like a vision of the night.

13335.label: Job 20:9
13335.text: The eye that has caught sight of him will not do so again,And no more will his place behold him.

13336.label: Job 20:10
13336.text: His own sons will seek the favor of lowly people,And his own hands will give back his valuable things.

13337.label: Job 20:11
13337.text: His own bones have been full of his youthful vigor,But with him it will lie down in mere dust.

13338.label: Job 20:12
13338.text: If what is bad tastes sweet in his mouth,If he causes it to melt away under his tongue,

13339.label: Job 20:13
13339.text: If he has compassion upon it and does not leave it,And if he keeps holding it back in the midst of his palate,

13340.label: Job 20:14
13340.text: His food itself will certainly be changed in his own intestines;It will be the gall of cobras within him.

13341.label: Job 20:15
13341.text: Wealth he has swallowed down, but he will vomit it up;God will drive it out from his very belly.

13342.label: Job 20:16
13342.text: The venom of cobras he will suck;The tongue of a viper will kill him.

13343.label: Job 20:17
13343.text: He will never see the watercourses, Torrential streams of honey and butter.

13344.label: Job 20:18
13344.text: He will be giving back [his] acquired property and will not swallow [it] down;Like wealth from his trade, but which he will not enjoy.

13345.label: Job 20:19
13345.text: For he has crushed to pieces, he has left lowly ones;He has snatched away a house itself that he did not proceed to build.

13346.label: Job 20:20
13346.text: For he will certainly know no ease in his belly;By means of his desirable things he will not escape.

13347.label: Job 20:21
13347.text: There is nothing left over for him to devour;That is why his well-being will not endure.

13348.label: Job 20:22
13348.text: While his plenty is at its peak he will be feeling anxious; All the power of misfortune itself will come against him.

13349.label: Job 20:23
13349.text: Let it occur that, to fill his belly,He will send his burning anger upon him And will rain [it] upon him, into his bowels.

13350.label: Job 20:24
13350.text: He will run away from armor of iron;A bow of copper will cut him up.

13351.label: Job 20:25
13351.text: A missile itself will even go out through his back,And a glittering weapon out through his gall; Frightful objects will go against him.

13352.label: Job 20:26
13352.text: All darkness will be reserved for his treasured things;A fire that no one fanned will eat him up; It will go badly with a survivor in his tent.

13353.label: Job 20:27
13353.text: Heaven will uncover his error, And earth will be in revolt against him.

13354.label: Job 20:28
13354.text: A heavy shower will roll his house away; There will be things poured forth on the day of his anger.

13355.label: Job 20:29
13355.text: This is the share of the wicked man from God, Even his stated inheritance from God.”

13356.label: Job 21:1
13356.text: And Job proceeded to answer and say:

13357.label: Job 21:2
13357.text: “Listen, YOU men, attentively to my word,And let this become YOUR consolation.

13358.label: Job 21:3
13358.text: Put up with me, and I myself shall speak;And after my speaking you may [each] deride.

13359.label: Job 21:4
13359.text: As for me, is my concern [expressed] to man?Or why is it that my spirit does not get impatient?

13360.label: Job 21:5
13360.text: Turn YOUR faces to me and stare in amazement,And put [YOUR] hand upon [YOUR] mouth.

13361.label: Job 21:6
13361.text: And if I have remembered, I have also become disturbed,And shuddering has taken hold of my flesh.

13362.label: Job 21:7
13362.text: Why is it that the wicked themselves keep living, Have grown old, also have become superior in wealth?

13363.label: Job 21:8
13363.text: Their offspring are firmly established with them in their sight,And their descendants before their eyes.

13364.label: Job 21:9
13364.text: Their houses are peace itself, free from dread, And the rod of God is not upon them.

13365.label: Job 21:10
13365.text: His own bull actually impregnates, and it does not waste semen;His cow brings forth and suffers no abortion.

13366.label: Job 21:11
13366.text: They keep sending out their young boys just like a flock,And their own male children go skipping about.

13367.label: Job 21:12
13367.text: They continue raising [their voice] with the tambourine and harp, And keep rejoicing at the sound of the pipe.

13368.label: Job 21:13
13368.text: They spend their days in good times, And in a moment down to Sheʹol they descend.

13369.label: Job 21:14
13369.text: And they say to the [true] God, ‘Turn away from us! And in the knowledge of your ways we have found no delight.

13370.label: Job 21:15
13370.text: What does the Almighty amount to, that we should serve him, And how do we benefit ourselves in that we have come in touch with him?’

13371.label: Job 21:16
13371.text: Look! Their well-being is not in their own power. The very counsel of wicked ones has kept far from me.

13372.label: Job 21:17
13372.text: How many times is the lamp of the wicked ones extinguished, And [how many times] does their disaster come upon them?[How many times] in his anger does he apportion destruction?

13373.label: Job 21:18
13373.text: Do they become like straw before a wind, And like chaff that a storm wind has stolen away?

13374.label: Job 21:19
13374.text: God himself will store up one’s hurtfulness for one’s own sons; He will reward him that he may know [it].

13375.label: Job 21:20
13375.text: His eyes will see his decay,And from the rage of the Almighty he will drink.

13376.label: Job 21:21
13376.text: For what will his delight be in his house after him,When the number of his months will really be cut in two?

13377.label: Job 21:22
13377.text: Will he teach knowledge even to God, When that One himself judges high ones?

13378.label: Job 21:23
13378.text: This very one will die during his full self-sufficiency, When he is altogether carefree and at ease;

13379.label: Job 21:24
13379.text: [When] his own thighs have become full of fatAnd the very marrow of his bones is being kept moist.

13380.label: Job 21:25
13380.text: And this other one will die with a bitter soulWhen he has not eaten of good things.

13381.label: Job 21:26
13381.text: Together in the dust they will lie down And maggots themselves will form a cover over them.

13382.label: Job 21:27
13382.text: Look! I well know the thoughts of YOU menAnd the schemes with which YOU would act violently against me.

13383.label: Job 21:28
13383.text: For YOU say, ‘Where is the house of the noble one,And where is the tent, the tabernacles of wicked ones?’

13384.label: Job 21:29
13384.text: Have YOU not asked those traveling over the roads?And do YOU not carefully inspect their very signs,

13385.label: Job 21:30
13385.text: That at the day of disaster an evil one is spared, At the day of fury he is delivered?

13386.label: Job 21:31
13386.text: Who will tell him of his way to his very face? And for what he himself has done who will reward him?

13387.label: Job 21:32
13387.text: As for him, to the graveyard he will be brought, And over a tomb a vigil will be kept.

13388.label: Job 21:33
13388.text: To him the clods of earth of a torrent valley will certainly become sweet, And after him he will drag all mankind, And those before him were without number.

13389.label: Job 21:34
13389.text: So how vainly YOU men try to comfort me, And YOUR very replies do remain as unfaithfulness!”

13390.label: Job 22:1
13390.text: And Elʹi·phaz the Teʹman·ite proceeded to answer and say:

13391.label: Job 22:2
13391.text: “Can an able-bodied man be of use to God himself, That anyone having insight should be of use toward him?

13392.label: Job 22:3
13392.text: Does the Almighty have any delight in that you are righteous, Or any gain in that you make your way blameless?

13393.label: Job 22:4
13393.text: For your reverence will he reprove you,Will he come with you into the judgment?

13394.label: Job 22:5
13394.text: Is not your own badness too much already, And will there be no end to your errors?

13395.label: Job 22:6
13395.text: For you seize a pledge from your brothers without cause, And you strip off even the garments of naked people.

13396.label: Job 22:7
13396.text: You do not give the tired one a drink of water,And from the hungry one you hold back bread.

13397.label: Job 22:8
13397.text: As for a man of strength, the land is his, And one who is treated with partiality himself dwells in it.

13398.label: Job 22:9
13398.text: Widows you have sent away empty-handed,And the arms of fatherless boys are crushed.

13399.label: Job 22:10
13399.text: That is why bird traps are all around you, And sudden dread disturbs you;

13400.label: Job 22:11
13400.text: Or darkness, [so that] you cannot see,And a heaving mass of water itself covers you.

13401.label: Job 22:12
13401.text: Is not God the height of heaven? Also see the sum total of the stars, that they are high.

13402.label: Job 22:13
13402.text: And yet you have said: ‘What does God really know?Through thick gloom can he judge?

13403.label: Job 22:14
13403.text: Clouds are a concealment place for him so that he does not see,And on the vault of heaven he walks about.’

13404.label: Job 22:15
13404.text: Will you keep to the very way of long agoThat hurtful men have trodden,

13405.label: Job 22:16
13405.text: [Men] who have been snatched away before their time, Whose foundation is poured away just as a river,

13406.label: Job 22:17
13406.text: Who are saying to the [true] God: ‘Turn away from us! And what can the Almighty accomplish against us?’

13407.label: Job 22:18
13407.text: Yet he himself has filled their houses with good things; And the very counsel of wicked ones has kept far from me.

13408.label: Job 22:19
13408.text: The righteous ones will see and rejoice, And the innocent one himself will hold them in derision:

13409.label: Job 22:20
13409.text: ‘Truly our antagonists have been effaced;And what is left of them a fire will certainly eat up.’

13410.label: Job 22:21
13410.text: Acquaint yourself, please, with him, and keep peace;Thereby good things will come to you.

13411.label: Job 22:22
13411.text: Take, please, the law from his own mouth,And put his sayings in your heart.

13412.label: Job 22:23
13412.text: If you return to the Almighty, you will be built up;[If] you will keep unrighteousness far from your tent,

13413.label: Job 22:24
13413.text: And [if] there is a placing of precious ore in the dustAnd gold of Oʹphir in the rock of torrent valleys,

13414.label: Job 22:25
13414.text: The Almighty also will indeed become your precious ores,And silver, the choicest, to you.

13415.label: Job 22:26
13415.text: For then in the Almighty you will find your exquisite delight, And you will raise your face to God himself.

13416.label: Job 22:27
13416.text: You will make entreaty to him, and he will hear you; And your vows you will pay.

13417.label: Job 22:28
13417.text: And you will decide on something, and it will stand for you;And upon your ways light will certainly shine.

13418.label: Job 22:29
13418.text: For there must be a humiliation when you speak arrogantly; But one with downcast eyes he will save.

13419.label: Job 22:30
13419.text: He will rescue an innocent man, And you will certainly be rescued for the cleanness of your hands.”

13420.label: Job 23:1
13420.text: And Job proceeded to answer and say:

13421.label: Job 23:2
13421.text: “Even today my state of concern is rebelliousness;My own hand is heavy on account of my sighing.

13422.label: Job 23:3
13422.text: O that I really knew where I might find him! I would come clear to his fixed place.

13423.label: Job 23:4
13423.text: I would present before him a case of justice,And my mouth I would fill with counterarguments;

13424.label: Job 23:5
13424.text: I would know the words with which he answers me,And I would consider what he says to me.

13425.label: Job 23:6
13425.text: Would he with an abundance of power contend with me?O no! Surely he himself would pay heed to me.

13426.label: Job 23:7
13426.text: There the upright one himself will certainly set matters straight with him,And I would go safe forever from my judge.

13427.label: Job 23:8
13427.text: Look! To the east I go, and he is not there;And back again, and I cannot discern him;

13428.label: Job 23:9
13428.text: To the left where he is working, but I cannot behold [him];He turns aside to the right, but I do not see [him].

13429.label: Job 23:10
13429.text: For he well knows the way I take. [After] he has tested me out, I shall come forth as gold itself.

13430.label: Job 23:11
13430.text: Of his steps my foot has laid hold;His way I have kept, and I do not deviate.

13431.label: Job 23:12
13431.text: [From] the commandment of his lips I do not move away. I have treasured up the sayings of his mouth more than what is prescribed for me.

13432.label: Job 23:13
13432.text: And he is in one [mind], and who can resist him? And his own soul has a desire, and he will do [it].

13433.label: Job 23:14
13433.text: For he will carry out completely what is prescribed for me, And things like these are many with him.

13434.label: Job 23:15
13434.text: That is why I feel disturbed because of him;I show myself attentive and am in dread of him.

13435.label: Job 23:16
13435.text: Even God himself has made my heart timid, And the Almighty himself has disturbed me.

13436.label: Job 23:17
13436.text: For I have not been put to silence because of darkness,Nor because gloom has covered my own face.

13437.label: Job 24:1
13437.text: “Why is it that times have not been stored up by the Almighty himself, And the very ones knowing him have not beheld his days?

13438.label: Job 24:2
13438.text: There are those who move back boundary marks; A drove they have snatched away, that they may shepherd [it].

13439.label: Job 24:3
13439.text: They drive off even the male ass of fatherless boys;They seize the widow’s bull as a pledge.

13440.label: Job 24:4
13440.text: They turn aside the poor ones from the way; At the same time the afflicted of the earth have kept themselves hidden.

13441.label: Job 24:5
13441.text: Look! [As] zebras in the wildernessThey have gone forth in their activity, looking for food.The desert plain [gives] to each one bread for the boys.

13442.label: Job 24:6
13442.text: In the field its fodder they harvest,And the vineyard of the wicked one they hastily despoil.

13443.label: Job 24:7
13443.text: Naked, they pass the night without a garment, And without any covering in the cold.

13444.label: Job 24:8
13444.text: From the rainstorm of the mountains they get drenched,And because there is no shelter they have to hug a rock.

13445.label: Job 24:9
13445.text: They snatch away a fatherless boy even from the breast, And what is on the afflicted one they take as a pledge.

13446.label: Job 24:10
13446.text: Naked, they have to go about without a garment,And, hungry, they have to carry the reaped ears.

13447.label: Job 24:11
13447.text: Between the terrace walls they pass the noontime; Winepresses they have to tread, and yet they go thirsty.

13448.label: Job 24:12
13448.text: From out of the city the dying keep groaning,And the soul of deadly wounded ones cries for help; And God himself considers [it] not as anything improper.

13449.label: Job 24:13
13449.text: As for them, they proved to be among the rebels against light; They did not recognize its ways,And they did not dwell in its roadways.

13450.label: Job 24:14
13450.text: At daylight the murderer gets up,He proceeds to slay the afflicted and the poor one; And during the night he becomes a regular thief.

13451.label: Job 24:15
13451.text: As for the eye of the adulterer, it has watched for evening darkness, Saying, ‘No eye will behold me!’ And over his face he puts a covering.

13452.label: Job 24:16
