13452.text: In the darkness he has dug into houses;By day they must keep themselves locked in.They have not known daylight.

13453.label: Job 24:17
13453.text: For morning is the same as deep shadow for them,For they recognize what the sudden terrors of deep shadow are.

13454.label: Job 24:18
13454.text: He is swift on the surface of the waters.Their tract of land will be cursed in the earth. He will not turn toward the way of the vineyards.

13455.label: Job 24:19
13455.text: The drought, also the heat, snatch away the snow waters;So does Sheʹol those who have sinned!

13456.label: Job 24:20
13456.text: The womb will forget him, the maggot will sweetly suck him, He will be remembered no more. And unrighteousness will be broken just like a tree.

13457.label: Job 24:21
13457.text: He is having dealings with a barren woman who does not bear,And with a widow, to whom he does no good.

13458.label: Job 24:22
13458.text: And he will certainly draw away strong people by his power;He will rise up and not be sure of his life.

13459.label: Job 24:23
13459.text: He will grant him to become confident that he may support himself;And his eyes will be upon their ways.

13460.label: Job 24:24
13460.text: They have become high up a little while, then they are no more, And they have been brought low; like everyone else they are plucked off,And like the head of an ear of grain they are cut off.

13461.label: Job 24:25
13461.text: So really now, who will make me out a liarOr reduce my word to nothing?”

13462.label: Job 25:1
13462.text: And Bilʹdad the Shuʹhite proceeded to answer and say:

13463.label: Job 25:2
13463.text: “Rulership and dreadfulness are with him; He is making peace on his heights.

13464.label: Job 25:3
13464.text: Is there any number to his troops?And upon whom does his light not rise?

13465.label: Job 25:4
13465.text: So how can mortal man be in the right before God, Or how can one born of a woman be clean?

13466.label: Job 25:5
13466.text: Look! There is even the moon, and it is not bright;And the stars themselves have not proved clean in his eyes.

13467.label: Job 25:6
13467.text: How much less so mortal man, who is a maggot,And a son of man, who is a worm!”

13468.label: Job 26:1
13468.text: And Job proceeded to answer and say:

13469.label: Job 26:2
13469.text: “O how much help you have been to one without power!O [how] you have saved an arm that is without strength!

13470.label: Job 26:3
13470.text: How much you have advised one that is without wisdom, And you have made practical wisdom itself known to the multitude!

13471.label: Job 26:4
13471.text: To whom have you told words,And whose breath has come forth from you?

13472.label: Job 26:5
13472.text: Those impotent in death keep tremblingBeneath the waters and those residing in them.

13473.label: Job 26:6
13473.text: Sheʹol is naked in front of him, And [the place of] destruction has no covering.

13474.label: Job 26:7
13474.text: He is stretching out the north over the empty place, Hanging the earth upon nothing;

13475.label: Job 26:8
13475.text: Wrapping up the waters in his clouds, So that the cloud mass is not split under them;

13476.label: Job 26:9
13476.text: Enclosing the face of the throne, Spreading out over it his cloud.

13477.label: Job 26:10
13477.text: He has described a circle upon the face of the waters, To where light ends in darkness.

13478.label: Job 26:11
13478.text: The very pillars of heaven shake,And they are amazed because of his rebuke.

13479.label: Job 26:12
13479.text: By his power he has stirred up the sea, And by his understanding he has broken the stormer to pieces.

13480.label: Job 26:13
13480.text: By his wind he has polished up heaven itself, His hand has pierced the gliding serpent.

13481.label: Job 26:14
13481.text: Look! These are the fringes of his ways, And what a whisper of a matter has been heard of him!But of his mighty thunder who can show an understanding?”

13482.label: Job 27:1
13482.text: And Job proceeded again to lift up his proverbial utterance and went on to say:

13483.label: Job 27:2
13483.text: “As God lives, who has taken away my judgment, And as the Almighty [lives], who has made my soul bitter,

13484.label: Job 27:3
13484.text: While my breath is yet whole within me,And the spirit of God is in my nostrils,

13485.label: Job 27:4
13485.text: My lips will speak no unrighteousnessAnd my own tongue will mutter no deceit!

13486.label: Job 27:5
13486.text: It is unthinkable on my part that I should declare YOU men righteous! Until I expire I shall not take away my integrity from myself!

13487.label: Job 27:6
13487.text: On my justness I have laid hold, and I shall not let it go; My heart will not taunt [me] for any of my days.

13488.label: Job 27:7
13488.text: Let my enemy become in every way a wicked man, And the one revolting against me really a wrongdoer.

13489.label: Job 27:8
13489.text: For what is the hope of an apostate in case he cuts [him] off, In case God carries off his soul from him?

13490.label: Job 27:9
13490.text: Will God hear an outcry of hisIn case distress comes upon him?

13491.label: Job 27:10
13491.text: Or in the Almighty will he find exquisite delight?Will he call to God at all times?

13492.label: Job 27:11
13492.text: I shall instruct YOU men by the hand of God;That which is with the Almighty I shall not hide.

13493.label: Job 27:12
13493.text: Look! YOU yourselves have all of YOU seen visions;So why is it that YOU show yourselves utterly vain?

13494.label: Job 27:13
13494.text: This is the share of the wicked man from God; And the inheritance of the tyrants they will receive from the Almighty himself.

13495.label: Job 27:14
13495.text: If his sons become many, it is for a sword; And his descendants themselves will not have enough food.

13496.label: Job 27:15
13496.text: His own survivors will be buried during a deadly plague, And their own widows will not weep.

13497.label: Job 27:16
13497.text: If he should pile up silver like dust itself,And he should prepare attire just as if clay,

13498.label: Job 27:17
13498.text: He would prepare, but the righteous would be the one to clothe himself, And in the silver the innocent would be the one to have a share.

13499.label: Job 27:18
13499.text: He has built his house like a mere moth,And like a booth that a watchman has made.

13500.label: Job 27:19
13500.text: Rich he will lie down, but nothing will be gathered; His eyes he has opened, but there will be nothing.

13501.label: Job 27:20
13501.text: Like waters sudden terrors will overtake him; At night a storm wind will certainly steal him away.

13502.label: Job 27:21
13502.text: An east wind will carry him off and he will go away,And it will whirl him away from his place.

13503.label: Job 27:22
13503.text: And it will hurl itself at him and have no compassion; From its power he will without fail try to run away.

13504.label: Job 27:23
13504.text: One will clap his hands at him And will whistle at him from his place.

13505.label: Job 28:1
13505.text: “Indeed, for silver there exists a place to find itAnd a place for gold that they refine;

13506.label: Job 28:2
13506.text: Iron itself is taken from the very dust And [from] stone copper is being poured out.

13507.label: Job 28:3
13507.text: An end to the darkness he has set;And to every limit he is searching out Stone in the gloom and deep shadow.

13508.label: Job 28:4
13508.text: He has sunk a shaft far from where [people] reside as aliens, Places forgotten far from the foot;Some of mortal men have swung down, they have dangled.

13509.label: Job 28:5
13509.text: As for the earth, out of it food goes forth; But underneath it, it has been upturned as if by fire.

13510.label: Job 28:6
13510.text: Its stones are the place of the sapphire, And it has gold dust.

13511.label: Job 28:7
13511.text: A pathway—no bird of prey has known it,Nor has the eye of a black kite caught sight of it.

13512.label: Job 28:8
13512.text: The majestic wild beasts have not trodden it down solid;The young lion has not paced over it.

13513.label: Job 28:9
13513.text: Upon the flint he has thrust out his hand;He has overthrown mountains from [their] root;

13514.label: Job 28:10
13514.text: Into the rocks he has channeled water-filled galleries, And all precious things his eye has seen.

13515.label: Job 28:11
13515.text: The places from which rivers trickled he has dammed up, And the concealed thing he brings forth to the light.

13516.label: Job 28:12
13516.text: But wisdom—where can it be found, And where, now, is the place of understanding?

13517.label: Job 28:13
13517.text: Mortal man has not come to know its valuation, And it is not found in the land of those living.

13518.label: Job 28:14
13518.text: The watery deep itself has said,‘It is not in me!’The sea too has said, ‘It is not with me!’

13519.label: Job 28:15
13519.text: Pure gold cannot be given in exchange for it, And silver cannot be weighed out as its price.

13520.label: Job 28:16
13520.text: It cannot be paid for with gold of Oʹphir, With the rare onyx stone and the sapphire.

13521.label: Job 28:17
13521.text: Gold and glass cannot be compared to it,Nor is any vessel of refined gold an exchange for it.

13522.label: Job 28:18
13522.text: Coral and rock crystal themselves will not be mentioned,But a bagful of wisdom is worth more than [one full of] pearls.

13523.label: Job 28:19
13523.text: The topaz of Cush cannot be compared to it;It cannot be paid for even with gold in its purity.

13524.label: Job 28:20
13524.text: But wisdom itself—from where does it come, And where, now, is the place of understanding?

13525.label: Job 28:21
13525.text: It has been hidden even from the eyes of everyone alive, And from the flying creatures of the heavens it has been concealed.

13526.label: Job 28:22
13526.text: Destruction and death themselves have said,‘With our ears we have heard a report of it.’

13527.label: Job 28:23
13527.text: God is the One who has understood its way, And he himself has known its place,

13528.label: Job 28:24
13528.text: For he himself looks to the very ends of the earth; Under the whole heavens he sees,

13529.label: Job 28:25
13529.text: To make a weight for the wind, While he has proportioned the waters themselves by a measure;

13530.label: Job 28:26
13530.text: When he made for the rain a regulation, And a way for the thunderous storm cloud,

13531.label: Job 28:27
13531.text: Then it was that he saw [wisdom] and proceeded to tell about it;He prepared it and also searched it through.

13532.label: Job 28:28
13532.text: And he went on to say to man, ‘Look! The fear of Jehovah —that is wisdom, And to turn away from bad is understanding.’”

13533.label: Job 29:1
13533.text: And Job proceeded again to lift up his proverbial utterance and went on to say:

13534.label: Job 29:2
13534.text: “O that I were as in the lunar months of long ago, As in the days when God was guarding me;

13535.label: Job 29:3
13535.text: When he caused his lamp to shine upon my head,[When] I would walk [through] darkness by his light;

13536.label: Job 29:4
13536.text: Just as I happened to be in the days of my prime, When intimacy with God was at my tent;

13537.label: Job 29:5
13537.text: When the Almighty was yet with me,[When] my attendants were all around me!

13538.label: Job 29:6
13538.text: When I washed my steps in butter,And the rock kept pouring out streams of oil for me;

13539.label: Job 29:7
13539.text: When I went forth to the gate by the town, In the public square I would prepare my seat!

13540.label: Job 29:8
13540.text: The boys saw me and hid themselves,And even the aged ones rose up, they stood.

13541.label: Job 29:9
13541.text: Princes themselves restrained words,And the palm they would put upon their mouth.

13542.label: Job 29:10
13542.text: The voice of the leaders themselves was hidden,And their very tongue cleaved to their palate.

13543.label: Job 29:11
13543.text: For the ear itself listened and proceeded to pronounce me happy,And the eye itself saw and proceeded to bear witness for me.

13544.label: Job 29:12
13544.text: For I would rescue the afflicted one crying for help, And the fatherless boy and anyone that had no helper.

13545.label: Job 29:13
13545.text: The blessing of the one about to perish—upon me it would come,And the heart of the widow I would make glad.

13546.label: Job 29:14
13546.text: With righteousness I clothed myself, and it was clothing me. My justice was like a sleeveless coat—and a turban.

13547.label: Job 29:15
13547.text: Eyes I became to the blind one; And feet to the lame one I was.

13548.label: Job 29:16
13548.text: I was a real father to the poor ones; And the legal case of one whom I did not know—I would examine it.

13549.label: Job 29:17
13549.text: And I would break the jawbones of the wrongdoer, And from his teeth I would tear away the prey.

13550.label: Job 29:18
13550.text: And I used to say, ‘Within my nest I shall expire, And like the grains of sand I shall multiply [my] days.

13551.label: Job 29:19
13551.text: My root is opened for the waters, And dew itself will stay overnight upon my bough.

13552.label: Job 29:20
13552.text: My glory is fresh with me,And my bow in my hand will shoot repeatedly.’

13553.label: Job 29:21
13553.text: To me they listened; and they waited,And they would keep silent for my counsel.

13554.label: Job 29:22
13554.text: After my word they would not speak again,And upon them my word would drip.

13555.label: Job 29:23
13555.text: And they waited for me as for the rain, And their mouth they opened wide for the spring rain.

13556.label: Job 29:24
13556.text: I would smile at them—they would not believe [it]—And the light of my face they would not cast down.

13557.label: Job 29:25
13557.text: I would choose the way for them, and I was sitting as head;And I resided as a king among [his] troops, As one who comforts the mourners.

13558.label: Job 30:1
13558.text: “And now they have laughed at me, Those younger in days than I am, Whose fathers I would have refusedTo place with the dogs of my flock.

13559.label: Job 30:2
13559.text: Even the power of their hands—of what use was it to me?In them vigor has perished.

13560.label: Job 30:3
13560.text: Because of want and hunger they are sterile,Gnawing at a waterless region, [Where] yesterday there were storm and desolation.

13561.label: Job 30:4
13561.text: They were plucking the salt herb by the bushes,And the root of broom trees was their food.

13562.label: Job 30:5
13562.text: From the community they would be driven away; People would shout at them as at a thief.

13563.label: Job 30:6
13563.text: [They have] to reside on the very slope of torrent valleys,In holes of the dust and in rocks.

13564.label: Job 30:7
13564.text: Among the bushes they would cry out;Under the nettles they would huddle together.

13565.label: Job 30:8
13565.text: Sons of the senseless one, also sons of the nameless one,They have been scourged out of the land.

13566.label: Job 30:9
13566.text: And now I have become even the theme of their song, And I am to them for a byword.

13567.label: Job 30:10
13567.text: They have detested me, they have kept themselves far from me; And from my face they did not hold back [their] spit.

13568.label: Job 30:11
13568.text: For he loosened [my] own bowstring and proceeded to humble me,And the bridle they left loose on my account.

13569.label: Job 30:12
13569.text: At [my] right hand they rise up as a brood;My feet they have let go,But they proceeded to cast up against me their disastrous barriers.

13570.label: Job 30:13
13570.text: They have torn down my roadways;They were beneficial only for adversity to me, Without their having any helper.

13571.label: Job 30:14
13571.text: As through a wide gap they proceed to come;Under a storm they have rolled along.

13572.label: Job 30:15
13572.text: Sudden terrors have been turned upon me;My noble bearing is chased like the wind, And like a cloud my salvation has passed away.

13573.label: Job 30:16
13573.text: And now my soul is poured out within me; Days of affliction take hold upon me.

13574.label: Job 30:17
13574.text: At night my very bones have been bored through [and dropped] from off me,And [pains] gnawing me do not take any rest.

13575.label: Job 30:18
13575.text: By the abundance of power my garment takes on a change;Like the collar of my long garment it engirdles me.

13576.label: Job 30:19
13576.text: He has brought me down to the clay,So that I show myself like dust and ashes.

13577.label: Job 30:20
13577.text: I cry to you for help, but you do not answer me; I have stood, that you might show yourself attentive to me.

13578.label: Job 30:21
13578.text: You change yourself to become cruel to me; With the full might of your hand you harbor animosity toward me.

13579.label: Job 30:22
13579.text: You lift me to the wind, you cause me to ride [it];Then you dissolve me with a crash.

13580.label: Job 30:23
13580.text: For I well know that to death you will make me turn back, And to the house of meeting for everyone living.

13581.label: Job 30:24
13581.text: Only no one thrusts his hand out against a mere heap of ruins, Nor during one’s decay is there a cry for help respecting those things.

13582.label: Job 30:25
13582.text: Certainly I have wept for the one having a hard day; My soul has grieved for the poor one.

13583.label: Job 30:26
13583.text: Although for good I waited, yet bad came; And I kept awaiting the light, but gloom came.

13584.label: Job 30:27
13584.text: My own intestines were made to boil and did not keep silent;Days of affliction confronted me.

13585.label: Job 30:28
13585.text: Saddened I walked about when there was no sunlight; I got up in the congregation, I kept crying for help.

13586.label: Job 30:29
13586.text: A brother to jackals I became,And a companion to the daughters of the ostrich.

13587.label: Job 30:30
13587.text: My very skin became black [and dropped] off me,And my very bones became hot from dryness.

13588.label: Job 30:31
13588.text: And my harp came to be merely for mourning,And my pipe for the voice of weeping ones.

13589.label: Job 31:1
13589.text: “A covenant I have concluded with my eyes. So how could I show myself attentive to a virgin?

13590.label: Job 31:2
13590.text: And what portion is there from God above, Or inheritance from the Almighty from on high?

13591.label: Job 31:3
13591.text: Is there not disaster for a wrongdoer, And misfortune for those practicing what is hurtful?

13592.label: Job 31:4
13592.text: Does he not himself see my ways And count even all my steps?

13593.label: Job 31:5
13593.text: If I have walked with [men of] untruth, And my foot hastens to deception,

13594.label: Job 31:6
13594.text: He will weigh me in accurate scales And God will get to know my integrity.

13595.label: Job 31:7
13595.text: If my stepping deviates from the way, Or my heart has walked merely after my eyes, Or any defect has stuck in my own palms,

13596.label: Job 31:8
13596.text: Let me sow seed and someone else eat, And let my own descendants be rooted out.

13597.label: Job 31:9
13597.text: If my heart has been enticed toward a woman, And I kept lying in wait at the very entranceway of my companion,

13598.label: Job 31:10
13598.text: Let my wife do the grinding for another man,And over her let other men kneel down.

13599.label: Job 31:11
13599.text: For that would be loose conduct,And that would be an error for [attention by] the justices.

13600.label: Job 31:12
13600.text: For that is a fire that would eat clear to destruction, And among all my produce it would take root.

13601.label: Job 31:13
13601.text: If I used to refuse the judgment of my slave manOr of my slave girl in their case at law with me,

13602.label: Job 31:14
13602.text: Then what can I do when God rises up?And when he calls for an accounting, what can I answer him?

13603.label: Job 31:15
13603.text: Did not the One making me in the belly make him, And did not just One proceed to prepare us in the womb?

13604.label: Job 31:16
13604.text: If I used to hold back the lowly ones from [their] delight, And the eyes of the widow I would cause to fail,

13605.label: Job 31:17
13605.text: And I used to eat my morsel by myself,While the fatherless boy did not eat from it

13606.label: Job 31:18
13606.text: (For from my youth he grew up with me as with a father,And from the belly of my mother I kept leading her);

13607.label: Job 31:19
13607.text: If I used to see anyone perishing from having no garment, Or that the poor one had no covering;

13608.label: Job 31:20
13608.text: If his loins did not bless me, Nor from the shorn wool of my young rams he would warm himself;

13609.label: Job 31:21
13609.text: If I waved my hand to and fro against the fatherless boy, When I would see [need of] my assistance in the gate,

13610.label: Job 31:22
13610.text: Let my own shoulder blade fall from its shoulder,And let my own arm be broken from its upper bone.

13611.label: Job 31:23
13611.text: For disaster from God was a dread to me,And against his dignity I could not hold out.

13612.label: Job 31:24
13612.text: If I have put gold as my confidence,Or to gold I have said, ‘You are my trust!’

13613.label: Job 31:25
13613.text: If I used to rejoice because my property was much, And because my hand had found a lot of things;

13614.label: Job 31:26
13614.text: If I used to see the light when it would flash forth,Or the precious moon walking along,

13615.label: Job 31:27
13615.text: And my heart began to be enticed in secrecy And my hand proceeded to kiss my mouth,

13616.label: Job 31:28
13616.text: That too would be an error for [attention by] the justices,For I should have denied the [true] God above.

13617.label: Job 31:29
13617.text: If I used to rejoice at the extinction of one intensely hating me, Or I felt excited because evil had found him—

13618.label: Job 31:30
13618.text: And I did not allow my palate to sinBy asking for an oath against his soul.

13619.label: Job 31:31
13619.text: If the men of my tent did not say,‘Who can produce anyone that has not been satisfied from food of his?’ —

13620.label: Job 31:32
13620.text: Outside no alien resident would spend the night; My doors I kept open to the path.

13621.label: Job 31:33
13621.text: If like an earthling man I covered over my transgressions By hiding my error in my shirt pocket—

13622.label: Job 31:34
13622.text: Because I would suffer a shock at a large crowd,Or the contempt itself of families would terrorize meAnd I would keep silent, I would not go out of the entrance.

13623.label: Job 31:35
13623.text: O that I had someone listening to me, That according to my signature the Almighty himself would answer me! Or that the individual in the case at law with me had written a document itself!

13624.label: Job 31:36
13624.text: Surely upon my shoulder I would carry it;I would bind it around me like a grand crown.

13625.label: Job 31:37
13625.text: The number of my steps I would tell him; Like a leader I would approach him.

13626.label: Job 31:38
13626.text: If against me my own ground would cry for aid,And together its furrows themselves would weep;

13627.label: Job 31:39
13627.text: If its fruitage I have eaten without money, And the soul of its owners I have caused to pant,

13628.label: Job 31:40
13628.text: Instead of wheat let the thorny weed go forth, And instead of barley stinking weeds.” The words of Job have come to an end.

13629.label: Job 32:1
13629.text: So these three men ceased from answering Job, for he was righteous in his own eyes.

13630.label: Job 32:2
13630.text: But the anger of E·liʹhu the son of Barʹa·chel the Buzʹite of the family of Ram came to be hot. Against Job his anger blazed over his declaring his own soul righteous rather than God.

13631.label: Job 32:3
13631.text: Also, against his three companions his anger blazed over the fact that they had not found an answer but they proceeded to pronounce God wicked.

13632.label: Job 32:4
13632.text: And E·liʹhu himself had waited for Job with words, because they were older than he was in days.

13633.label: Job 32:5
13633.text: And E·liʹhu gradually saw that there was no answer in the mouth of the three men, and his anger kept getting hotter.

13634.label: Job 32:6
13634.text: And E·liʹhu the son of Barʹa·chel the Buzʹite proceeded to answer and say: “Young I am in daysAnd YOU men are aged. That is why I drew back and was afraidTo declare my knowledge to YOU men.

13635.label: Job 32:7
13635.text: I said, ‘Days themselves should speak,And a multitude of years are what should make wisdom known.’

13636.label: Job 32:8
13636.text: Surely it is the spirit in mortal menAnd the breath of the Almighty [that] gives them understanding.

13637.label: Job 32:9
13637.text: It is not those merely abundant in days that prove wise, Nor those just old that understand judgment.

13638.label: Job 32:10
13638.text: Therefore I said, ‘Do listen to me.I shall declare my knowledge, even I.’

13639.label: Job 32:11
13639.text: Look! I have waited for the words of YOU men,I kept giving ear to YOUR reasonings, Until YOU could search for words [to say].

13640.label: Job 32:12
13640.text: And to YOU I kept my attention turned,And here there is no one reproving Job,None of YOU answering his sayings,

13641.label: Job 32:13
13641.text: That YOU may not say, ‘We have found wisdom; It is God that drives him away, not a man.’

13642.label: Job 32:14
13642.text: As he has not arrayed words against me,So with the sayings of YOU men I shall not reply to him.

13643.label: Job 32:15
13643.text: They have been terrified, they have answered no more;Words have moved away from them.

13644.label: Job 32:16
13644.text: And I have waited, for they do not continue speaking;For they stood still, they answered no more.

13645.label: Job 32:17
13645.text: I shall give in answer my part, even I;I shall declare my knowledge, even I;

13646.label: Job 32:18
13646.text: For I have become full of words;Spirit has brought pressure upon me in my belly.

13647.label: Job 32:19
13647.text: Look! My belly is like wine that has no vent;Like new skin bottles it wants to burst open.

13648.label: Job 32:20
13648.text: Let me speak that it may be a relief to me.I shall open my lips that I may answer.

13649.label: Job 32:21
13649.text: Let me not, please, show partiality to a man; And on an earthling man I shall not bestow a title;

13650.label: Job 32:22
13650.text: For I certainly do not know how I can bestow a title;Easily my Maker would carry me away.

13651.label: Job 33:1
13651.text: “Now, however, O Job, please hear my words, And to all my speaking do give ear.

13652.label: Job 33:2
13652.text: Look, please! I have to open my mouth;My tongue with my palate has to speak.

13653.label: Job 33:3
13653.text: My sayings are the uprightness of my heart, And knowledge is what my lips do utter sincerely.

13654.label: Job 33:4
13654.text: God’s own spirit made me, And the Almighty’s own breath proceeded to bring me to life.

13655.label: Job 33:5
13655.text: If you are able, make reply to me,Array [words] before me; do take your station.

13656.label: Job 33:6
13656.text: Look! I am to the [true] God just what you are; From the clay I was shaped, I too.

13657.label: Job 33:7
13657.text: Look! No frightfulness in me will terrify you,And no pressure by me will be heavy upon you.

13658.label: Job 33:8
13658.text: Only you have said in my ears,And the sound of [your] words I kept hearing,

13659.label: Job 33:9
13659.text: ‘I am pure without transgression; Clean I am, and I have no error.

13660.label: Job 33:10
13660.text: Look! Occasions for opposition to me he finds,He takes me for an enemy of his.

13661.label: Job 33:11
13661.text: He puts my feet in the stocks, He watches all my paths.’

13662.label: Job 33:12
13662.text: Look! In this you have not been in the right, I answer you;For God is much more than mortal man.

13663.label: Job 33:13
13663.text: Why is it against him that you contended, Because all your words he does not answer?

13664.label: Job 33:14
13664.text: For God speaks once,And twice —though one does not regard it—

13665.label: Job 33:15
13665.text: In a dream, a vision of the night,When deep sleep falls upon men,During slumbers upon the bed.

13666.label: Job 33:16
13666.text: It is then that he uncovers the ear of men, And on exhortation to them he puts his seal,

13667.label: Job 33:17
13667.text: To turn aside a man from his deed, And that he may cover pride itself from an able-bodied man.

13668.label: Job 33:18
13668.text: He keeps his soul back from the pit And his life from passing away by a missile.

13669.label: Job 33:19
13669.text: And he is actually reproved with pain upon his bed,And the quarreling of his bones is continual.

13670.label: Job 33:20
13670.text: And his life certainly makes bread loathsome, And his own soul desirable food.

13671.label: Job 33:21
13671.text: His flesh wastes away from sight,And his bones that were not seen certainly grow bare.

13672.label: Job 33:22
13672.text: And his soul draws near to the pit, And his life to those inflicting death.

13673.label: Job 33:23
13673.text: If there exists for him a messenger, A spokesman, one out of a thousand,To tell to man his uprightness,

13674.label: Job 33:24
13674.text: Then he favors him and says,‘Let him off from going down into the pit! I have found a ransom!

13675.label: Job 33:25
13675.text: Let his flesh become fresher than in youth; Let him return to the days of his youthful vigor.’

13676.label: Job 33:26
13676.text: He will make entreaty to God that he may take pleasure in him, And he will see his face with joyful shouting,And He will restore His righteousness to mortal man.

13677.label: Job 33:27
13677.text: He will sing to men and say,‘I have sinned; and what is upright I have perverted,And it certainly was not the proper thing for me.

13678.label: Job 33:28
13678.text: He has redeemed my soul from passing into the pit, And my life itself will see the light.’

13679.label: Job 33:29
13679.text: Look! All these things God performs,Two times, three times, in the case of an able-bodied man,

13680.label: Job 33:30
13680.text: To turn his soul back from the pit, That he may be enlightened with the light of those living.

13681.label: Job 33:31
13681.text: Pay attention, O Job! Listen to me!Keep silent, and I myself shall continue speaking.

13682.label: Job 33:32
13682.text: If there are any words [to say], make reply to me;Speak, for I have taken delight in your righteousness.

13683.label: Job 33:33
13683.text: If there are none, you yourself listen to me; Keep silent, and I shall teach you wisdom.”

13684.label: Job 34:1
13684.text: And E·liʹhu continued to answer and say:

13685.label: Job 34:2
13685.text: “Listen, YOU wise ones, to my words;And YOU who know, give ear to me.

13686.label: Job 34:3
13686.text: For the ear itself makes a test of words, Just as the palate tastes when eating.

13687.label: Job 34:4
13687.text: Judgment let us choose for ourselves;Let us know among ourselves what is good.

13688.label: Job 34:5
13688.text: For Job has said, ‘I certainly am in the right, But God himself has turned aside the judgment of me.

13689.label: Job 34:6
13689.text: Against my own judgment do I tell lies?My severe wound is incurable though there is no transgression.’

13690.label: Job 34:7
13690.text: What able-bodied man is like Job, [Who] drinks up derision like water?

13691.label: Job 34:8
13691.text: And he is certainly on his way to companionship with practicers of what is hurtfulAnd to walking with men of wickedness.

13692.label: Job 34:9
13692.text: For he has said, ‘An able-bodied man does not profit By his taking pleasure in God.’

13693.label: Job 34:10
13693.text: Therefore, YOU men of heart, listen to me.Far be it from the [true] God to act wickedly, And the Almighty to act unjustly!

13694.label: Job 34:11
13694.text: For [according to] the way earthling man acts he will reward him,And according to the path of man he will cause it to come upon him.

13695.label: Job 34:12
13695.text: Yes, for a fact, God himself does not act wickedly, And the Almighty himself does not pervert judgment.

13696.label: Job 34:13
13696.text: Who has assigned to him the earth,And who has appointed [to him] the productive land, even all of it?

13697.label: Job 34:14
13697.text: If he sets his heart upon anyone,[If] that one’s spirit and breath he gathers to himself,

13698.label: Job 34:15
13698.text: All flesh will expire together,And earthling man himself will return to the very dust.

13699.label: Job 34:16
13699.text: So if [you have] understanding, do listen to this;Do give ear to the sound of my words.

13700.label: Job 34:17
13700.text: Really will anyone hating justice control, And if a powerful one is righteous will you pronounce [him] wicked?

13701.label: Job 34:18
13701.text: Shall one say to a king, ‘You are good for nothing’? To nobles, ‘You are wicked’?

13702.label: Job 34:19
13702.text: [There is One] who has not shown partiality to princesAnd has not given more consideration to the noble one than to the lowly one,For all of them are the work of his hands.

13703.label: Job 34:20
13703.text: In a moment they die, even in the middle of the night; The people shake back and forth and pass away,And powerful ones depart by no hand.

13704.label: Job 34:21
13704.text: For his eyes are upon the ways of man, And all his steps he sees.

13705.label: Job 34:22
13705.text: There is no darkness nor any deep shadowFor those practicing what is hurtful to conceal themselves there.

13706.label: Job 34:23
13706.text: For he sets no appointed time for any manTo go to God in judgment.

13707.label: Job 34:24
13707.text: He breaks powerful ones without any investigation,And he makes others stand up instead of them.

13708.label: Job 34:25
13708.text: Therefore he recognizes what their works are, And he does overthrow [them] at night, and they get crushed.

13709.label: Job 34:26
13709.text: As wicked ones he does slap themIn the place of onlookers;

13710.label: Job 34:27
13710.text: For the reason that they have turned aside from following him, And none of his ways have they considered,

13711.label: Job 34:28
13711.text: So as to cause the outcry of the lowly one to come to him;And so he hears the outcry of the afflicted ones.

13712.label: Job 34:29
13712.text: When he himself causes quietness, who, then, can condemn?And when he conceals [his] face, who can behold him,Whether it is toward a nation or toward a man, it being the same thing?

13713.label: Job 34:30
13713.text: So that an apostate man may not reign, Nor there be snares of the people.

13714.label: Job 34:31
13714.text: For will anyone actually say to God himself,‘I have borne, although I do not act corruptly;

13715.label: Job 34:32
13715.text: Although I behold nothing, instruct me yourself;If any unrighteousness I have committed,I shall not do [it] again’?

13716.label: Job 34:33
13716.text: Will he make good for it from your standpoint because you do refuse [judgment],Because you yourself choose, and not I?Even what you well know, speak.

13717.label: Job 34:34
13717.text: Men of heart themselves will say to me—Even a wise able-bodied man that is listening to me,

13718.label: Job 34:35
13718.text: ‘Job himself speaks without knowledge, And his words are without [his] having insight.’

13719.label: Job 34:36
13719.text: My father, let Job be tested out to the limitOver his replies among men of hurtfulness.

13720.label: Job 34:37
13720.text: For on top of his sin he adds revolt; Among us he claps [his hands] and multiplies his sayings against the [true] God!”

13721.label: Job 35:1
13721.text: And E·liʹhu continued answering and saying:

13722.label: Job 35:2
13722.text: “Is this what you have regarded as justice?You have said, ‘My righteousness is more than God’s.’

13723.label: Job 35:3
13723.text: For you say, ‘Of what use is it to you? What benefit do I have more than by my sinning?’

13724.label: Job 35:4
13724.text: I myself shall reply to youAnd to your companions with you.

13725.label: Job 35:5
13725.text: Look up to heaven and see,And behold the clouds, [that] they are indeed higher than you.

13726.label: Job 35:6
13726.text: If you actually sin, what do you accomplish against him? And [if] your revolts actually increase, what do you do to him?

13727.label: Job 35:7
13727.text: If you are really in the right, what do you give him,Or what does he receive from your own hand?

13728.label: Job 35:8
13728.text: Your wickedness may be against a man like you, And your righteousness to a son of earthling man.

13729.label: Job 35:9
13729.text: Because of the multitude of oppressions they keep calling for aid; They keep crying for help because of the arm of the great ones.

13730.label: Job 35:10
13730.text: And yet no one has said, ‘Where is God my Grand Maker, The One giving melodies in the night?’

13731.label: Job 35:11
13731.text: He is the One teaching us more than the beasts of the earth, And he makes us wiser than even the flying creatures of the heavens.

13732.label: Job 35:12
13732.text: There they keep crying out, but he does not answer, Because of the pride of the bad ones.

13733.label: Job 35:13
13733.text: Only the untruth God does not hear, And the Almighty himself does not behold it.

13734.label: Job 35:14
13734.text: How much less, then, when you say you do not behold him! The legal case is before him, and so you should wait anxiously for him.

13735.label: Job 35:15
13735.text: And now because his anger has not called for an accounting, He has also not taken note of the extreme rashness.

13736.label: Job 35:16
13736.text: And Job himself opens his mouth wide simply for nothing;Without knowledge he multiplies mere words.”

13737.label: Job 36:1
13737.text: And E·liʹhu proceeded to say further:

13738.label: Job 36:2
13738.text: “Have patience with me a little while, and I shall declare to youThat there are yet words [to say] for God.

13739.label: Job 36:3
13739.text: I shall carry my knowledge from far off,And to my Fashioner I shall ascribe righteousness.

13740.label: Job 36:4
13740.text: For my words are for a fact no falsehood;The One perfect in knowledge is with you.

13741.label: Job 36:5
13741.text: Look! God is mighty and will not reject;[He is] mighty in power of heart;

13742.label: Job 36:6
13742.text: He will not preserve anyone wicked alive, But the judgment of the afflicted ones he will give.

13743.label: Job 36:7
13743.text: He will not take away his eyes from anyone righteous; Even kings on the throne —He will also seat them forever, and they will be exalted.

13744.label: Job 36:8
13744.text: And if they are bound in fetters, They are captured with ropes of affliction.

13745.label: Job 36:9
13745.text: Then he will tell them about the way they actAnd their transgressions, because they take a superior air.

13746.label: Job 36:10
13746.text: And he will uncover their ear to exhortation, And he will say that they should turn back from what is hurtful.

13747.label: Job 36:11
13747.text: If they obey and serve,They will finish their days in what is goodAnd their years in pleasantness.

13748.label: Job 36:12
13748.text: But if they do not obey, they will pass away even by a missile, And they will expire without knowledge.

13749.label: Job 36:13
13749.text: And those apostate in heart will themselves lay up anger. They should not cry for help because he has bound them.

13750.label: Job 36:14
13750.text: Their soul will die in youth itself, And their life among male temple prostitutes.

13751.label: Job 36:15
13751.text: He will rescue the afflicted one in his affliction,And he will uncover their ear in the oppression.

13752.label: Job 36:16
13752.text: And he will also certainly allure you from the mouth of distress! Broader space, not constraint, will be in its place,And the consolation of your table will be full of fatness.

13753.label: Job 36:17
13753.text: With the judicial sentence upon the wicked one you will certainly be filled;Judicial sentence and justice will themselves take hold.

13754.label: Job 36:18
13754.text: For [take care] that rage does not allure you into [spiteful] handclapping,And let not a large ransom itself lead you astray.

13755.label: Job 36:19
13755.text: Will your cry for help take effect? No, nor in distressEven all [your] powerful efforts.

13756.label: Job 36:20
13756.text: Do not pant for the night, For peoples to retreat [from] where they are.

13757.label: Job 36:21
13757.text: Be on your guard that you do not turn to what is hurtful, For this you have chosen rather than affliction.

13758.label: Job 36:22
13758.text: Look! God himself acts exaltedly with his power;Who is an instructor like him?

13759.label: Job 36:23
13759.text: Who has called his way to account against him, And who has said, ‘You have committed unrighteousness’?

13760.label: Job 36:24
13760.text: Remember that you should magnify his activity Of which men have sung.

13761.label: Job 36:25
13761.text: All mankind themselves have gazed upon it;Mortal man himself keeps looking from far off.

13762.label: Job 36:26
13762.text: Behold! God is more exalted than we can know; In number his years are beyond searching.

13763.label: Job 36:27
13763.text: For he draws up the drops of water; They filter as rain for his mist,

13764.label: Job 36:28
13764.text: So that the clouds trickle, They drip upon mankind abundantly.

13765.label: Job 36:29
13765.text: Indeed, who can understand the cloud layers,The crashings from his booth?

13766.label: Job 36:30
13766.text: Look! He has spread out over it his light, And the roots of the sea he has covered.

13767.label: Job 36:31
13767.text: For by them he pleads the cause of peoples; He gives food in abundance.

13768.label: Job 36:32
13768.text: In his hands he has covered over the lightning, And he lays a command upon it against an assailant.

13769.label: Job 36:33
13769.text: His booming tells about him, The livestock also concerning the one coming up.

13770.label: Job 37:1
13770.text: “Indeed at this my heart begins to tremble, And it leaps up from its place.

13771.label: Job 37:2
13771.text: Listen attentively, YOU men, to the rumbling of his voice, And the growling that goes forth from his mouth.

13772.label: Job 37:3
13772.text: Under the whole heavens he lets it loose,And his lightning is to the extremities of the earth.

13773.label: Job 37:4
13773.text: After it a sound roars;He thunders with the sound of his superiority, And he does not hold them back when his voice is heard.

13774.label: Job 37:5
13774.text: God thunders with his voice in a wonderful way,Doing great things that we cannot know.

13775.label: Job 37:6
13775.text: For to the snow he says, ‘Fall earthward,’ And [to] the downpour of rain, even [to] the downpour of his strong rains.

13776.label: Job 37:7
13776.text: On the hand of every earthling man he puts a sealFor every mortal man to know his work.

13777.label: Job 37:8
13777.text: And the wild beast comes into the ambush,And in its hiding places it dwells.

13778.label: Job 37:9
13778.text: Out of the interior room comes the storm windAnd out of the north winds the cold.

13779.label: Job 37:10
13779.text: By the breath of God the ice is given And the breadth of waters is under constraint.

13780.label: Job 37:11
13780.text: Yes, with moisture he burdens the cloud,His light scatters the cloud mass,

13781.label: Job 37:12
13781.text: And it is being turned round about by his steering [them] for their performanceWherever he commands them upon the face of the productive land of the earth.

13782.label: Job 37:13
13782.text: Whether for a rod or for his land Or for loving-kindness, he makes it produce effects.

13783.label: Job 37:14
13783.text: Do give ear to this, O Job;Stand still and show yourself attentive to the wonderful works of God.

13784.label: Job 37:15
13784.text: Do you know when God laid an appointment upon them, And when he caused the light of his cloud to beam?

13785.label: Job 37:16
13785.text: Do you know about the poisings of the cloud, The wonderful works of the One perfect in knowledge?

13786.label: Job 37:17
13786.text: How your garments are hotWhen the earth shows quietness from the south?

13787.label: Job 37:18
13787.text: With him can you beat out the skies Hard like a molten mirror?

13788.label: Job 37:19
13788.text: Let us know what we should say to him;We cannot produce [words] because of darkness.

13789.label: Job 37:20
13789.text: Should it be related to him that I would speak?Or has any man said that it will be communicated?

13790.label: Job 37:21
13790.text: And now they do not really see the light;It is brilliant in the skies,When a wind itself has passed by and proceeded to cleanse them.

13791.label: Job 37:22
13791.text: Out of the north golden splendor comes.Upon God dignity is fear-inspiring.

13792.label: Job 37:23
13792.text: As for the Almighty, we have not found him out; He is exalted in power, And justice and abundance of righteousness he will not belittle.

13793.label: Job 37:24
13793.text: Therefore let men fear him. He does not regard any who are wise in [their own] heart.”

13794.label: Job 38:1
13794.text: And Jehovah proceeded to answer Job out of the windstorm and say:

13795.label: Job 38:2
13795.text: “Who is this that is obscuring counselBy words without knowledge?

13796.label: Job 38:3
13796.text: Gird up your loins, please, like an able-bodied man,And let me question you, and you inform me.

13797.label: Job 38:4
13797.text: Where did you happen to be when I founded the earth? Tell [me], if you do know understanding.

13798.label: Job 38:5
13798.text: Who set its measurements, in case you know,Or who stretched out upon it the measuring line?

13799.label: Job 38:6
13799.text: Into what have its socket pedestals been sunk down,Or who laid its cornerstone,

13800.label: Job 38:7
13800.text: When the morning stars joyfully cried out together,And all the sons of God began shouting in applause?

13801.label: Job 38:8
13801.text: And [who] barricaded the sea with doors, Which began to go forth as when it burst out from the womb;

13802.label: Job 38:9
13802.text: When I put the cloud as its garmentAnd thick gloom as its swaddling band,

13803.label: Job 38:10
13803.text: And I proceeded to break up my regulation upon itAnd to set a bar and doors,

13804.label: Job 38:11
13804.text: And I went on to say, ‘This far you may come, and no farther; And here your proud waves are limited’?

13805.label: Job 38:12
13805.text: Was it from your days onward that you commanded the morning? Did you cause the dawn to know its place,

13806.label: Job 38:13
13806.text: To take hold on the extremities of the earth,That the wicked ones might be shaken out from it?

13807.label: Job 38:14
13807.text: It transforms itself like clay under a seal,And things take their station as in clothing.

13808.label: Job 38:15
13808.text: And from the wicked ones their light is held back, And the high arm itself gets broken.

13809.label: Job 38:16
13809.text: Have you come to the sources of the sea,Or in search of the watery deep have you walked about?

13810.label: Job 38:17
13810.text: Have the gates of death been uncovered to you,Or the gates of deep shadow can you see?

13811.label: Job 38:18
13811.text: Have you intelligently considered the broad spaces of the earth? Tell, if you have come to know it all.

13812.label: Job 38:19
13812.text: Where, now, is the way to where light resides? As for darkness, where, now, is its place,

13813.label: Job 38:20
13813.text: That you should take it to its boundaryAnd that you should understand the roadways to its house?

13814.label: Job 38:21
13814.text: Have you come to know because at that time you were being born, And [because] in number your days are many?

13815.label: Job 38:22
13815.text: Have you entered into the storehouses of the snow, Or do you see even the storehouses of the hail,

13816.label: Job 38:23
13816.text: Which I have kept back for the time of distress,For the day of fight and war?

13817.label: Job 38:24
13817.text: Where, now, is the way by which the light distributes itself,[And] the east wind scatters about upon the earth?

13818.label: Job 38:25
13818.text: Who has divided a channel for the floodAnd a way for the thunderous storm cloud,

13819.label: Job 38:26
13819.text: To make it rain upon the land where there is no man, [Upon] the wilderness in which there is no earthling man,

13820.label: Job 38:27
13820.text: To satisfy storm-stricken and desolate placesAnd to cause the growth of grass to sprout?

13821.label: Job 38:28
13821.text: Does there exist a father for the rain, Or who gave birth to the dewdrops?

13822.label: Job 38:29
13822.text: Out of whose belly does the ice actually come forth,And as for the hoarfrost of heaven, who indeed brings it to birth?

13823.label: Job 38:30
13823.text: The very waters keep themselves hidden as by stone,And the surface of the watery deep makes itself compact.

13824.label: Job 38:31
13824.text: Can you tie fast the bonds of the Kiʹmah constellation, Or can you loosen the very cords of the Keʹsil constellation?

13825.label: Job 38:32
13825.text: Can you bring forth the Mazʹza·roth constellation in its appointed time?And as for the Ash constellation alongside its sons, can you conduct them?

13826.label: Job 38:33
13826.text: Have you come to know the statutes of the heavens, Or could you put its authority in the earth?

13827.label: Job 38:34
13827.text: Can you raise your voice even to the cloud,So that a heaving mass of water itself may cover you?

13828.label: Job 38:35
13828.text: Can you send forth lightnings that they may goAnd say to you, ‘Here we are!’?

13829.label: Job 38:36
13829.text: Who put wisdom in the cloud layers, Or who gave understanding to the sky phenomenon?

13830.label: Job 38:37
13830.text: Who can exactly number the clouds in wisdom,Or the water jars of heaven—who can tip [them] over,

13831.label: Job 38:38
13831.text: When the dust pours out as into a molten mass,And the clods of earth themselves get stuck together?

13832.label: Job 38:39
13832.text: Can you hunt prey for a lion itselfAnd can you satisfy the lively appetite of young lions,

13833.label: Job 38:40
13833.text: When they crouch in the hiding places, [Or] keep lying in the covert for an ambush?

13834.label: Job 38:41
13834.text: Who prepares for the raven its food When its own young ones cry to God for help,[When] they keep wandering about because there is nothing to eat?

13835.label: Job 39:1
13835.text: “Have you come to know the appointed time for the mountain goats of the crag to give birth? Do you observe just when the hinds bring forth with birth pangs?

13836.label: Job 39:2
13836.text: Do you count the lunar months that they fulfill,Or have you come to know the appointed time that they give birth?

13837.label: Job 39:3
13837.text: They bow down when they cast forth their young ones,[When] they get rid of their pangs.

13838.label: Job 39:4
13838.text: Their sons become robust, they get big in the open field;They actually go forth and do not return to them.

13839.label: Job 39:5
13839.text: Who sent forth the zebra free,And who loosened the very bands of the wild ass,

13840.label: Job 39:6
13840.text: Whose house I have appointed the desert plainAnd whose dwelling places the salt country?

13841.label: Job 39:7
13841.text: It laughs at the turmoil of a town;The noises of a stalker it does not hear.

13842.label: Job 39:8
13842.text: It explores mountains for its pasturage And after every sort of green plant it seeks.

13843.label: Job 39:9
13843.text: Does a wild bull want to serve you, Or will it spend the night by your manger?

13844.label: Job 39:10
13844.text: Will you bind a wild bull fast with its ropes in the furrow,Or will it harrow low plains after you?

13845.label: Job 39:11
13845.text: Will you trust in it because its power is abundant,And will you leave your toil to it?

13846.label: Job 39:12
13846.text: Will you rely on it that it will bring back your seedAnd that it will gather to your threshing floor?

13847.label: Job 39:13
13847.text: Has the wing of the female ostrich flapped joyously,Or [has she] the pinions of a stork and the plumage?

13848.label: Job 39:14
13848.text: For she leaves her eggs to the earth itselfAnd in the dust she keeps them warm,

13849.label: Job 39:15
13849.text: And she forgets that some foot may crush themOr even a wild beast of the field may tread on them.

13850.label: Job 39:16
13850.text: She does treat her sons roughly, as if not hers —In vain is her toil [because she has] no dread.

13851.label: Job 39:17
13851.text: For God has made her forget wisdom,And he has not given her a share in understanding.

13852.label: Job 39:18
13852.text: At the time she flaps [her wings] on high,She laughs at the horse and at its rider.

13853.label: Job 39:19
13853.text: Can you give to the horse mightiness? Can you clothe its neck with a rustling mane?

13854.label: Job 39:20
13854.text: Can you cause it to leap like a locust?The dignity of its snorting is frightful.

13855.label: Job 39:21
13855.text: It paws in the low plain and exults in power;It goes forth to meet armor.

13856.label: Job 39:22
13856.text: It laughs at dread, and is not terrified; Nor does it turn back on account of a sword.

13857.label: Job 39:23
13857.text: Against it a quiver rattles,The blade of a spear and a javelin.

13858.label: Job 39:24
13858.text: With pounding and excitement it swallows up the earth,And it does not believe that it is the sound of a horn.

13859.label: Job 39:25
13859.text: As soon as the horn blows it says Aha!And from far off it smells the battle,The uproar of chiefs and the war cry.

13860.label: Job 39:26
13860.text: Is it owing to your understanding that the falcon soars up,That it spreads its wings to the south wind?

13861.label: Job 39:27
13861.text: Or is it at your order that an eagle flies upwardAnd that it builds its nest high up,

13862.label: Job 39:28
13862.text: That on a crag it resides and stays during the nightUpon the tooth of a crag and an inaccessible place?

13863.label: Job 39:29
13863.text: From there it has to search for food; Far into the distance its eyes keep looking.

13864.label: Job 39:30
13864.text: And its young ones themselves keep sipping up blood;And where the slain are, there it is.”

13865.label: Job 40:1
13865.text: And Jehovah proceeded to answer Job and say:

13866.label: Job 40:2
13866.text: “Should there be any contending of a faultfinder with the Almighty? Let the reprover of God himself answer it.”

13867.label: Job 40:3
13867.text: And Job went on to answer Jehovah and say:

13868.label: Job 40:4
13868.text: “Look! I have become of little account. What shall I reply to you?My hand I have put over my mouth.

13869.label: Job 40:5
13869.text: Once have I spoken, and I will not answer;And twice, and I will add nothing.”

13870.label: Job 40:6
13870.text: And Jehovah went on to answer Job out of the windstorm and say:

13871.label: Job 40:7
13871.text: “Gird up your loins, please, like an able-bodied man; I shall question you, and you inform me.

13872.label: Job 40:8
13872.text: Really, will you invalidate my justice?Will you pronounce me wicked in order that you may be in the right?

13873.label: Job 40:9
13873.text: Or do you have an arm like that of the [true] God, And with a voice like his can you make it thunder?

13874.label: Job 40:10
13874.text: Deck yourself, please, with superiority and highness; And with dignity and splendor may you clothe yourself.

13875.label: Job 40:11
13875.text: Let flow the furious outbursts of your anger, And see every one haughty and bring him low.

13876.label: Job 40:12
13876.text: See every one haughty, humble him, And tread down the wicked right where they are.

13877.label: Job 40:13
13877.text: Hide them together in the dust, Bind their very faces in the hidden place,

13878.label: Job 40:14
13878.text: And I, even I, shall commend you,Because your right hand can save you.

13879.label: Job 40:15
13879.text: Here, now, is Be·heʹmoth that I have made as well as you.Green grass it eats just as a bull does.

13880.label: Job 40:16
13880.text: Here, now, its power is in its hips,And its dynamic energy in the tendons of its belly.

13881.label: Job 40:17
13881.text: It bends down its tail like a cedar;The sinews of its thighs are interwoven.

13882.label: Job 40:18
13882.text: Its bones are tubes of copper;Its strong bones are like wrought-iron rods.

13883.label: Job 40:19
13883.text: It is the beginning of the ways of God; Its Maker can bring near his sword.

13884.label: Job 40:20
13884.text: For the mountains themselves bear their produce for it, And all the wild beasts of the field themselves play there.

13885.label: Job 40:21
13885.text: Under the thorny lotus trees it lies down,In the concealed place of reeds and the swampy place.

13886.label: Job 40:22
13886.text: The thorny lotus trees keep it blocked off with their shadow;The poplars of the torrent valley surround it.

13887.label: Job 40:23
13887.text: If the river acts violently, it does not run in panic.It is confident, although the Jordan should burst forth against its mouth.

13888.label: Job 40:24
13888.text: Before its eyes can anyone take it?With snares can anyone bore [its] nose?

13889.label: Job 41:1
13889.text: “Can you draw out Le·viʹa·than with a fishhook,Or with a rope can you hold down its tongue?

13890.label: Job 41:2
13890.text: Can you put a rush in its nostrils, Or with a thorn can you bore its jaws?

13891.label: Job 41:3
13891.text: Will it make many entreaties to you,Or will it say soft words to you?

13892.label: Job 41:4
13892.text: Will it conclude a covenant with you,That you may take it as a slave to time indefinite?

13893.label: Job 41:5
13893.text: Will you play with it as with a bird,Or will you tie it for your young girls?

13894.label: Job 41:6
13894.text: Will partners barter for it? Will they divide it up among tradesmen?

13895.label: Job 41:7
13895.text: Will you fill its skin with harpoons, Or its head with fish spears?

13896.label: Job 41:8
13896.text: Put your hand upon it.Remember the battle. Do not do it again.

13897.label: Job 41:9
13897.text: Look! One’s expectation about it will certainly be disappointed.One will also be hurled down at the mere sight of it.

13898.label: Job 41:10
13898.text: None is so audacious that he should stir it up.And who is it that can hold his ground before me?

13899.label: Job 41:11
13899.text: Who has given me something first, that I ought to reward him? Under the whole heavens it is mine.

13900.label: Job 41:12
13900.text: I shall not keep silent about its partsOr the matter of [its] mightiness and the grace of its proportions.

13901.label: Job 41:13
13901.text: Who has uncovered the face of its clothing?Into its double jaw who will enter?

13902.label: Job 41:14
13902.text: The doors of its face who has opened?Its teeth round about are frightful.

13903.label: Job 41:15
13903.text: Furrows of scales are its haughtiness,Closed as with a tight seal.

13904.label: Job 41:16
13904.text: One to the other they fit closely,And not even air can come in between them.

13905.label: Job 41:17
13905.text: Each one to the other they are stuck together;They grasp one another and cannot be separated.

13906.label: Job 41:18
13906.text: Its very sneezings flash forth light,And its eyes are like the beams of dawn.

13907.label: Job 41:19
13907.text: Out of its mouth there go lightning flashes,Even sparks of fire make their escape.

13908.label: Job 41:20
13908.text: Out of its nostrils smoke goes forth,Like a furnace set aflame even with rushes.

13909.label: Job 41:21
13909.text: Its soul itself sets coals ablaze,And even a flame goes forth out of its mouth.

13910.label: Job 41:22
13910.text: In its neck lodges strength,And before it despair leaps.

13911.label: Job 41:23
13911.text: The folds of its flesh do cling together;They are as a casting upon it, immovable.

13912.label: Job 41:24
13912.text: Its heart is cast like stone,Yes, cast like a lower millstone.

13913.label: Job 41:25
13913.text: Due to its rising up the strong get frightened; Due to consternation they get bewildered.

13914.label: Job 41:26
13914.text: Overtaking it, the sword itself does not prove equal,Nor spear, dart or arrowhead.

13915.label: Job 41:27
13915.text: It regards iron as mere straw,Copper as mere rotten wood.

13916.label: Job 41:28
13916.text: An arrow does not chase it away;The slingstones have been changed for it into mere stubble.

13917.label: Job 41:29
13917.text: A club has been regarded [by it] as mere stubble, And it laughs at the rattling of a javelin.

13918.label: Job 41:30
13918.text: As pointed earthenware fragments are its underparts;It spreads out a threshing instrument upon the mire.

13919.label: Job 41:31
13919.text: It causes the depths to boil just like a pot;It makes the very sea like an ointment pot.

13920.label: Job 41:32
13920.text: Behind itself it makes a pathway shine; One would regard the watery deep as gray-headedness.

13921.label: Job 41:33
13921.text: Upon the dust there is not the like of it,The one made to be without terror.

13922.label: Job 41:34
13922.text: Everything high it sees.It is king over all majestic wild beasts.”

13923.label: Job 42:1
13923.text: And Job proceeded to answer Jehovah and say:

13924.label: Job 42:2
13924.text: “I have come to know that you are able to do all things, And there is no idea that is unattainable for you.

13925.label: Job 42:3
13925.text: ‘Who is this that is obscuring counsel without knowledge?’ Therefore I talked, but I was not understandingThings too wonderful for me, which I do not know.

13926.label: Job 42:4
13926.text: ‘Hear, please, and I myself shall speak.I shall question you, and you inform me.’

13927.label: Job 42:5
13927.text: In hearsay I have heard about you,But now my own eye does see you.

13928.label: Job 42:6
13928.text: That is why I make a retraction,And I do repent in dust and ashes.”

13929.label: Job 42:7
13929.text: And it came about after Jehovah had spoken these words to Job, that Jehovah proceeded to say to Elʹi·phaz the Teʹman·ite: “My anger has grown hot against you and your two companions, for YOU men have not spoken concerning me what is truthful as has my servant Job.

13930.label: Job 42:8
13930.text: And now take for yourselves seven bulls and seven rams and go to my servant Job, and YOU men must offer up a burnt sacrifice in YOUR own behalf; and Job my servant will himself pray for YOU. His face only I shall accept so as not to commit disgraceful folly with YOU, for YOU have not spoken concerning me what is truthful, as has my servant Job.”

13931.label: Job 42:9
13931.text: Accordingly Elʹi·phaz the Teʹman·ite and Bilʹdad the Shuʹhite [and] Zoʹphar the Naʹa·ma·thite went and did just as Jehovah had spoken to them; and so Jehovah accepted Job’s face.

13932.label: Job 42:10
13932.text: And Jehovah himself turned back the captive condition of Job when he prayed in behalf of his companions, and Jehovah began to give in addition all that had been Job’s, in double amount.

13933.label: Job 42:11
13933.text: And there kept coming to him all his brothers and all his sisters and all those formerly knowing him, and they began to eat bread with him in his house and to sympathize with him and to comfort him over all the calamity that Jehovah had let come upon him; and they proceeded each one to give him a piece of money and each one a gold ring.

13934.label: Job 42:12
13934.text: As for Jehovah, he blessed the end of Job afterward more than his beginning, so that he came to have fourteen thousand sheep and six thousand camels and a thousand spans of cattle and a thousand she-asses.

13935.label: Job 42:13
13935.text: He also came to have seven sons and three daughters.

13936.label: Job 42:14
13936.text: And he went calling the name of the first Je·miʹmah and the name of the second Ke·ziʹah and the name of the third Kerʹen-hapʹpuch.

13937.label: Job 42:15
13937.text: And no women were found as pretty as Job’s daughters in all the land, and their father proceeded to give them an inheritance in among their brothers.

13938.label: Job 42:16
13938.text: And Job continued living after this a hundred and forty years and came to see his sons and his grandsons —four generations.

13939.label: Job 42:17
13939.text: And gradually Job died, old and satisfied with days.
